jobs.description:
COMPANY 🌱

RYZE was founded in 2019 by Andrée Werner and Rashad Hossain, out of a parents' basement 🏠, with a mission to change daily health, starting with the morning routine: a nutrient-dense mushroom coffee ☕🍄 delivering clean energy ⚡, mental clarity 🧠, and immune support 🛡️. Built on a Direct-to-Consumer foundation with a performance marketing engine, RYZE achieved hockey-stick growth 📈 and a community of over 1 million active subscribers. 🎉

DTC remains the foundation, but RYZE has expanded into mass retail 🛒, quickly becoming the #2 item in Target's overall coffee category and is now executing a multi-channel expansion, with a cross-category launch coming in early 2027 🚀.

RYZE is uniquely positioned to redefine how people think about daily wellness. ✨
We're a lean, fast-moving, mission-driven team who believe daily rituals create the foundation for living your greatest life, and we're just getting started! 🌱🔥

WHAT YOU'LL DO 🎯

We're looking for a Lifecycle Operations Manager to sit at the intersection of marketing strategy and technical execution — the person who takes lifecycle briefs and journey maps and turns them into live, tested, working flows in Klaviyo and Postscript. This is not a campaign coordinator role. This is the technical half of the lifecycle partnership: the person who interrogates the brief, surfaces the gaps, builds the logic layer, and keeps the stack healthy. You build things that work — and you know what it takes to keep them working.

Responsibilities will include:

Translate Strategy into Built Experiences

  • Take lifecycle briefs, journey maps, and campaign strategy and turn them into robust, tested, live flows in Klaviyo and Postscript — built and scheduled, not near-final drafts.

  • Interrogate the brief before you build it: surface gaps a strategist wouldn't think to specify — customers already in the flow, active subscribers, recent sends, no order history.

  • Tell Marketing when something isn't buildable as written — and come back with the version that is, or the work required to make it possible.

  • Configure the full logic layer: triggers, filters, conditional splits, profile property conditions, wait timing, smart sending, and suppression.

  • Coordinate email and SMS so channels complement rather than collide, and build the guardrails and governance that keep sending rules consistent as the program grows.

Build the Foundation That Makes It Possible

  • Own the technical health of our lifecycle stack — Klaviyo, Postscript, Shopify, and Recharge — including integration stability, data governance, and documentation that outlives any one person's memory.

  • Own the tracking layer end to end: verify that Shopify, Recharge, and on-site events land in Klaviyo with the right properties, on the right profile, at the right time. If Marketing wants to trigger on something we don't currently capture, you make it capturable.

  • Configure and troubleshoot webhooks, API-driven events, custom metrics, and profile properties.

  • Maintain source-of-truth definitions for the events, attributes, and segments the retention program runs on.

  • Drive operational efficiency by building reusable systems — modular templates, universal content blocks, dynamic content logic — so the tenth version of a journey takes a fraction of the time the first one did.

  • Lead the evaluation and onboarding of new capabilities with a clear view of impact vs. complexity.

Test It and Launch It

  • Own the pre-send QA standard for every email and SMS build: dynamic content and personalization across edge cases, link and UTM accuracy, alt text, dark mode, mobile, and rendering across major inbox clients.

  • QA the technical side of landing pages: form and popup behavior, consent capture, list assignment, redirects, mobile rendering, and whether tracking actually fires.

  • QA product and subscription configuration: variants, selling plans, discount and bundle logic, Recharge subscription rules, one-time vs. recurring behavior, and swap or upsell flows.

  • Operationalize A/B tests end to end: audience configuration, randomization, holdouts, and instrumentation that's actually measurable.

  • Help define clear experiment frameworks — success metrics, sample sizes, timelines — and make sure the implementation is technically sound so results mean something.

Keep It Running

  • Monitor flow health, delivery, and errors proactively. Broken things should surface on your dashboard, not in a post-mortem.

  • Find and fix silent failures before they become reporting problems: events that stopped firing, properties that drifted, duplicate or mis-identified profiles, integrations that quietly desynced.

  • Monitor sending health — bounce and complaint rates, list growth quality, suppression hygiene, sunset logic — and keep authentication and sending domain configuration in good standing.

  • Own reporting requirements for lifecycle ops: flow health, delivery and error monitoring, and experiment status.

  • Proactively consolidate or retire journeys that add operational complexity without adding return.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR 🔍

  • 2–4 years of hands-on experience in lifecycle / CRM operations at a DTC or ecommerce brand, working directly from marketing briefs.

  • Deep working knowledge of Klaviyo as your primary tool — flows, segments, templates, and integrations, not just campaign sends.

  • Hands-on experience with Shopify and Recharge, including how subscription data behaves and where it tends to break.

  • Experience with an SMS platform — Postscript preferred; Attentive, Klaviyo SMS, or similar considered.

  • Technical proficiency with HTML, CSS for email, and templating logic (Liquid or similar); comfortable reading, writing, and debugging dynamic content and personalization rules.

  • Demonstrated experience partnering with developers or data teams on integrations, event tracking, and troubleshooting. You can read an API doc, test an endpoint, and reason about a webhook payload without hand-holding.

  • Solid understanding of experiment design — control vs. test, holdouts, key metrics, avoiding bias — and its practical constraints in a live sending program.

  • Proven ability to manage multiple builds in parallel with clear prioritization and communication — and to tell a stakeholder what's realistic before committing to it.

PERSONAL CHARACTERISTICS 💫

  • Low-ego, team-first: The best idea wins, no matter whose it is

  • Self-starter: You see what needs doing and get after it, no waiting for direction

  • Comfortable in ambiguity: Fast pace and shifting priorities energize you rather than rattle you

  • Builder at heart: You're energized by a fast-moving environment where you help create the processes and playbooks, not just follow them

  • Mission-driven: You genuinely care about wellness and are excited to help build RYZE's next chapter


WHAT WE OFFER 🌟

Benefits

  • Competitive hourly or monthly contract compensation 💰

  • Fully remote, flexible work environment 🌍

  • Opportunity to work on high-impact performance creative for a fast-growing brand 🚀

  • Access to RYZE creative assets, tools, templates, and performance insights 🎨

jobs.description:
Please submit your CV in English and indicate your level of English proficiency.

Mindrift connects specialists with project-based AI opportunities for leading tech companies, focused on testing, evaluating, and improving AI systems. Participation is project-based, not permanent employment.

We're building a dataset to evaluate AI coding agents - how well a model handles real-world developer tasks.

You'll create challenging tasks and evaluation criteria within realistic simulated environments:

  • Build realistic developer environments - a virtual company with codebase, infrastructure, and context (tickets, docs, conversations) that forms a believable development history
  • Design tasks from intermediate states of these environments - craft the prompt, define what "solved" means, and ensure the task is solvable by an AI agent
  • Write tests that verify agent solutions - accept all valid approaches and reject incorrect ones, neither too strict nor too lenient
  • Iterate on tasks and tests based on QA feedback - review agent solutions, analyze failures, and refine until the evaluation is fair and robust

What this is NOT:

  • Not data labeling
  • Not prompt engineering
  • Not writing code from scratch - the agent writes most of the code; you guide and evaluate

What we look for:

  • 5+ years in software development
  • Core stack: Python (FastAPI), JavaScript/TypeScript (React), Docker, Postgres, Kafka, Redis
  • Experience writing tests (functional, integration)
  • English proficiency - B2+

Why this is hard:
Frontier models are already good at coding. Creating a task that genuinely challenges the best models is non-trivial. You need to deeply understand where models fail and what scenarios reveal the difference between a good and a bad solution. Tasks have many valid solutions - writing tests that accept all correct solutions and reject incorrect ones is harder than it sounds.

Requirements and benefits

Educational qualifications

  • A Master’s Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science / Data Analytics, Artificial Intelligence / Machine Learning, Computational Linguistics / Natural Language Processing (NLP), Information Systems or other related fields.
  • Bachelor’s degree is accepted if only candidate has 5 years of experience in the field.

Academic and/or Professional Experience

Candidates should have a minimum of 3 years of professional experience in related roles or domain - specifically for QA-automation/testing or cybersecurity roles

How it works
Apply → Pass qualification(s) → Join a project → Complete tasks → Get paid

Compensation:
Paid per accepted task. Your rate depends on the qualification tier you reach and how efficiently you complete tasks — up to the equivalent of $50/hr. Because payment is per task, a faster pace raises your effective hourly rate.

Why this freelance opportunity might be a great fit for you?

  • Take part in a part-time, remote, freelance project that fits around your primary professional or academic commitments.
  • Work on advanced AI projects and gain valuable experience that enhances your portfolio. - Influence how future AI models understand and communicate in your field of expertise.

This team owns the infrastructure layer between applications and foundation models: model access, routing, reliability, security integration, observability, and cost management behind a single governed interface. Sitting in the request path for every AI-powered application makes latency, reliability, and efficiency company-level outcomes rather than local ones.

This team also owns a measurement and attribution layer that makes consumption legible to the optimization capabilities that act on it, including intelligent routing, caching, context optimization, and capacity planning. We're looking for a Director of Data Science to own the strategy and technical leadership behind Mission Lane's credit acquisition models, reporting to the Sr. Director, Data Science.

The impact you'll make:

Someone hits submit on a credit card application, hopeful this is the “yes” that lets them start building toward something: a car, a home, a little more room to breathe. You'll lead the strategy and the team behind decisions like that one. Keeping every decision accurate and fair as circumstances shift makes this work interesting and rewarding, every day.

Mission Lane is young, but we’ve landed in an exciting, stable stretch of maturation: still moving toward what we’re going to become, with plenty of room for you to help shape it.

  • Technical leadership for the data scientists building and maintaining acquisition models, setting the bar for model design, code quality, and production rigor
  • Model risk and monitoring practices that keep acquisition models compliant, explainable, and accurate as underwriting conditions change

  • A growing scope as acquisitions-adjacent growth initiatives roll into the team, giving you room to shape how the function expands

jobs.title: Designer - Digitalist
jobs.excerpt: The main purpose of the Designer is to work on design-related tasks for Digitalist's assigned clients and projects, with the responsibility to create quality, effective, well-designed, and impactful visual work across websites, e-commerce stores, and paid and owned marketing channels that converts and drives sales for our clients.
jobs.description:
The main purpose of the Designer is to work on design-related tasks for Digitalist's assigned clients and projects, with the responsibility to create quality, effective, well-designed, and impactful visual work across websites, e-commerce stores, and paid and owned marketing channels that converts and drives sales for our clients.

As a Designer, you will work closely with Account Managers, developers, and specialists to conceptualize and design a variety of client deliverables. On the web side this means design concepts for WordPress and WooCommerce websites and online stores, landing pages, and conversion-focused UX and UI work that is clean to hand over to development. On the marketing side this means Facebook and Google ad creatives, email marketing designs, content marketing graphics, and social assets, all of which have to express the voice, style, look and feel, and overall design of the brand. This will involve having a deep understanding of clients' visual brand identities, communicating new ideas to the team (verbally and visually), implementing client feedback in your designs, and supporting the team throughout the design and editing process. You will need to be creative while working within the direction of your design briefs.

The Designer will report directly to the Design Lead and the Agency Director, and will also work closely with the development, marketing, and analytics sides of the team to ensure that all designs are created well and on time.

About the Role:

Mission statement:

The primary mission of our Designer is to maintain the high design standards of our company by playing an active role in the design and visual creation process across our range of clients and for our own marketing material.

As our Designer, this will include translating analysis and conversion goals into design concepts for client websites and online stores, designing performance creative and email campaigns that reflect each client's message, brand, and style, coming up with innovative design ideas, and ensuring that your work is of the highest standard and delivered on time. Our web process always starts with the goal of higher conversion and sales, so you will be designing to a commercial outcome rather than to a mood board.

General Responsibilities:

  • Creating design concepts for client websites and e-commerce stores (primarily WordPress and WooCommerce), including page templates, product and category pages, checkout flows, and landing pages, using professional design tools (including Figma)
  • Preparing clean, well-structured, developer-ready files and handovers, including responsive states, components, spacing, and typography rules, and staying available to the developers through implementation
  • Creating high-quality, on-brand creatives for Facebook Ads and Google Ads, including static, motion-lite, and iteration variants for testing
  • Designing email marketing campaigns and flows, along with content marketing and social assets, in line with each client's brand identity
  • Creating and developing visually pleasing yet marketing-oriented and effective concepts in design
  • Working from data and analysis (heatmaps, analytics, tracking findings, test results) and turning that input into design decisions that lift conversion
  • Understanding the visual brand identity of various clients and being able to advise your Account Managers on potential design ideas, improvements, and optimizations
  • Understanding and communicating design ideas (in writing, verbally, and with the use of visuals) to other team members and, when needed, to clients
  • Receiving and implementing feedback and design changes to projects you have worked on
  • Assisting Account Managers with all tasks in Figma, including implementing edits and helping to design professional reports when needed
  • Being part of a team of both expert and less experienced designers, being able to work as a group when needed, and being able to stick to deadlines and deliver high-quality finished designs on time
  • Being well-versed in current design platforms and software, and open to learning how to effectively and productively use new tools
  • Designing marketing materials for our own company's marketing efforts when needed (including blog posts, social media content, and email assets)
  • Constantly educating yourself and developing your technical skills to enhance your expertise
  • Working on various tasks, initiatives, and projects as delegated by the Design Lead
  • Continuously working to improve the design-driven results for your assigned clients
  • Keeping contact with your assigned clients, including assisting in and attending regular meetings with them alongside the Account Managers
  • Maintaining high design standards across the agency and making sure the set targets for your assigned clients are met in terms of their design requirements
  • Participating in training and skill-building sessions for the Design Team to improve skills, performance, and overall expertise
  • Participating in the Design Team's group calls
  • Continuously working to discover industry-wide best practices and standards and presenting your findings to the Design Lead and the Agency Director
  • Being available to assist with all internal design-related needs from other parts of the team
  • Directly reporting to the Design Lead and the Agency Director (in that structural order)

Position Specs:

  • Fully remote position
  • Full-time commitment, Central Europe standard office hours (Monday to Friday)
  • Fixed-rate monthly salary
  • Receive contractor status after signing our non-disclosure agreement
  • Exclusivity agreement (nullifying the possibility to work in a position of a similar nature while working for Digitalist)
  • Committing to a 30-day notice period after the first month
  • Regular performance reviews every 9-12 months, with the first one being after 3-6 months

Requirements

About you:

Profile:

The ideal candidate must be an experienced designer with an established portfolio showcasing elevated, effective, and on-brand work for a variety of clients, stores, and niches. That portfolio should show both sides of this role: website and e-commerce design that shipped and performed, and marketing creative such as ad sets and email campaigns. Having been part of a design team before is a must for this role.

The Designer should have solid experience with Figma and the Adobe Creative Suite, and should be comfortable designing for WordPress and WooCommerce builds, including an understanding of what a theme or page builder can realistically implement. Experience with Elementor or a comparable builder, basic HTML and CSS literacy, familiarity with an email platform such as Klaviyo or Mailchimp, motion or short-form video editing, and previous agency experience are all considered a plus.

The Designer must be able to act swiftly upon receiving urgent requests and be able to work consistently with high levels of accountability. The right person will be professional and also have extensive graphic design experience, as well as strong communication, presentation, organizational, time management, and interpersonal skills to effectively deliver work of high quality promptly. You will need to possess a refined aesthetic sense, strong typography skills, effective time management skills, a high level of responsiveness, and the ability to take action and work fast to implement changes and solve design-related problems.

Familiarity with tools such as Figma, Adobe Creative Suite, WordPress, Slack, a time-tracking tool, a project management tool, and the Google Workspace Suite is a must for this role. You should feel comfortable working in a remote environment. Availability, accountability, professionalism, responsiveness, and consistency are highly important factors for us, so the Designer should display these qualities when it comes to workload commitments and general availability during office hours.

Key traits for this position:

Showing great attention to detail, being organized and structured, being both big-picture and process-oriented, possessing good communication and interpersonal skills, and having a grasp of current design-related digital marketing trends and best practices in our industry. The right person will also possess strong design and typography skills with a high level of visual intelligence. You need to be able to understand your assigned clients' brand identity, style, and voice and create designs that reflect that, and you need to be comfortable being held to a conversion or sales outcome rather than only to how the work looks. The ability to use design styles consistently across various client accounts is a must. Being accountable, approachable, and well-organized is key for this role.

Key Requirements:

  • At least 5 years of experience working as a Designer in a professional role or similar experience in a design role at another agency (preference will be given to candidates who have worked with remote teams and team members from different countries, or who have agency experience)
  • An in-depth understanding and proficiency in a variety of design tools, including Figma and the Adobe Creative Suite, and a willingness to learn how to use other design tools in the future
  • Demonstrable experience designing websites and online stores that were actually built and launched, ideally on WordPress or WooCommerce
  • Demonstrable experience designing paid social and search creative, and email marketing designs
  • Experience with Elementor or a comparable page builder, basic HTML and CSS literacy, an email platform such as Klaviyo or Mailchimp, motion or short-form video editing, or previous agency experience are considered a plus
  • Having an established design portfolio showcasing elevated, effective, and on-brand designs for a variety of clients, stores, and niches
  • Must possess the ability to create designs for a variety of clients, regardless of their brand and niche
  • A refined aesthetic sense and strong typography skills to be able to create and deliver quality work
  • Have the ability to take action and work fast to implement changes and solve design-related problems
  • Must possess strong communication, presentation, organizational, time management, and interpersonal skills to effectively deliver work of high quality promptly
  • Should be able to perform both repetitive and miscellaneous tasks while maintaining a high level of accuracy in your work
  • Must be highly accountable, responsive, and have an excellent ability to meet deadlines
  • Great aptitude for working with people, problem-solving, and thinking critically and analytically
  • Must be able to work on video editing tasks, mostly for UGC content
  • Possesses a growth and results-driven mindset, and can handle and implement constructive criticism
  • Any remote work experience is a major advantage
  • Excellent interpersonal skills to clearly and effectively communicate with clients as well as with the marketing, development, and analytics people on our team
  • Familiarity with working autonomously and managing your time (remote work experience is a plus)
  • Must be available and responsive during Central Europe standard office hours, Monday to Friday
  • Must have a stable internet connection and a laptop or PC, as well as be able to attend virtual video conferences
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English (you must be fluent in English, although English does not have to be your native language)
  • Slovenian, Croatian, or Serbian is a plus given our client base, but it is not a requirement
  • Being open to receiving feedback and constructive criticism and improving on it, as well as giving feedback of a similar nature productively to your team

jobs.excerpt: About PacasoPacaso exists to enrich lives by making second home ownership possible and enjoyable for more people.
jobs.description:
About Pacaso

Pacaso exists to enrich lives by making second home ownership possible and enjoyable for more people. We've reimagined the second home category — pairing a thoughtfully designed co-ownership model with simplified financials, equitable scheduling, and dedicated local property management, so owners get the joy of a true second home without the hassle.

Since launch, Pacaso has facilitated more than $1.2 billion in gross real estate transactions and service fees across 40+ destinations in the U.S., Mexico, and Europe — including Aspen, Lake Tahoe, Napa, Malibu, Palm Springs, Cabo, Paris, London, and most recently Florence, Milan, and Rome. We've raised over $300 million in cumulative equity funding, closed the largest real estate Regulation A+ offering of 2025, and reserved the Nasdaq ticker PCSO as we build toward a public listing.

Our work has been featured in The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, Fortune, Forbes, CNBC, Bloomberg, and others.

Recognition

We're a Certified Great Place to Work and have been honored for both our culture and our category-defining work:

  • No. 5, Forbes America's Best Startup Employers (2026) — our second consecutive Top 10 ranking
  • Newsweek's America's Greatest Startup Workplaces (2025)
  • Winner, 2025 Inman Best of Proptech Awards — Consumer Experience & Marketplace Innovation
  • Fortune & Great Place To Work Best Workplaces in Real Estate (2024)
  • Best Workplace in the Bay Area™ (2023)
  • LinkedIn Top Startup (2022) · Glassdoor Best Places to Work, #6 (2022)

Why this role exists

Pacaso created co-ownership of the second home: all the ownership a family actually uses, in the places they love, without the weight of owning it. The old way is whole ownership, with all of its cost and all of its operating burden for a few weeks of use a year. Moving a family from one to the other is among the most considered decisions they will ever make, and most of that consideration happens between conversations with Sales. Lifecycle marketing is how Pacaso shows up well in that time.

Three audiences make the case. Many people discover Pacaso years before they are ready to buy, and re-engaging them at the right moment is one of our largest growth levers. Active prospects deserve communication that matches the care of the decision they are weighing. And our Owners, the most credible proof the model works, should hear from us with the same taste as the homes they own. This is demand Pacaso has already earned. The job is to convert it.

IN BRIEF Own how Pacaso communicates with everyone in our database, from first inquiry through years of ownership.

What you'll own

You will shape lifecycle strategy with the VP of Marketing and build it yourself. Together you will decide how each of these audiences should experience Pacaso over time; you will then open Iterable and make it real. You are the most senior lifecycle practitioner at the company, reporting to the VP of Marketing and working closely with brand, creative, analytics and Sales.

Marketing at Pacaso runs lean and AI-native. We hire owners who multiply themselves with AI rather than teams that grow by headcount. You should already work this way, with AI drafting your variants, scoring your segments and checking your campaigns while your own judgment goes to strategy, taste and measurement.

REACTIVATION

Many buyers begin this journey long before they are ready. You will decide when and how to re-engage past inquiries, what would genuinely bring someone back and how a re-engaged buyer gets handed to Sales cleanly. It is the fastest path this role has to funded volume, and it is where you will start.

PROSPECT NURTURE

A Pacaso purchase can take months of consideration. You will design how a prospect experiences those months: what they hear after a first inquiry, how a specific home or market stays present in their thinking and what earns the consultation. Segmentation, personalization and disciplined testing are your instruments. Pacaso does not discount or rush its buyers, so the program earns attention through relevance rather than urgency.

OWNER COMMUNICATIONS

Owners are the heart of the brand and the source of our referrals and resales. Working with the owner experience team, you will define what Owners hear from Pacaso and when, from onboarding through arrival moments, home updates and referral programs, and set the governance that keeps those touches coordinated across teams. The standard is that every message an Owner receives feels like it came from the same hand that welcomed them home.

PLATFORM AND MEASUREMENT

You own the Iterable instance end to end: data architecture, deliverability, channel setup across email, SMS and push, and the connections to our CRM and data warehouse. You define lifecycle success in numbers (reactivation rate, conversion to consultation, owner engagement and revenue influenced) and report it to leadership monthly.

Who you are

You have led lifecycle for a considered, high-value purchase, in real estate, financial services, travel or something similar, and you never stopped building.

Specifically:

  • 8+ years in lifecycle, CRM or retention marketing, with several of them owning the strategy.
  • Expert in Iterable.
  • Journeys, segmentation, catalogs, templating and deliverability are muscle memory.
  • AI-native in practice. You can point to programs where AI changed your speed or your results.
  • Comfortable in SQL and fluent in funnel math, incrementality and holdout design.
  • A writer's ear. You can draft a subject line that converts and catch a line that reads off voice for a brand built on restraint.
  • Experienced working with Sales on lead scoring, handoff and pipeline reporting.

Compensation - $160,000 to $175,000 depending on experience and location plus equity

Why You'll Love Working Here

We invest in our Crew the way we invest in our homes — thoughtfully, generously, and with care.

  • Competitive base salary and meaningful equity — every Crew member shares in what we're building
  • Discretionary time off — take the rest you need, when you need it
  • Premium medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your family
  • Sponsored memberships to One Medical, Peloton, and WellHub for whole-person, modern healthcare
  • 401(k) to help you build long-term security
  • Paid parental leave for primary and secondary caregivers
  • Home office stipend and a monthly internet and cell phone reimbursement to set you up for great remote work
  • Quarterly team gatherings and ongoing learning and development investment

Our Commitment

Pacaso is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of every race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, ability, and background — including veterans and individuals with disabilities. We believe a Crew as diverse as the owners we serve makes Pacaso stronger, and we're committed to building a workplace where every voice belongs.

We treat grants as a growth strategy. Funding is pursued because it opens new markets, underwrites new programs and additional levels of care, and expands access in communities that need it. Because a number of our field, outreach, and patient access positions are funded in whole or in part by grant dollars, this role also carries business development responsibility. You will assist the Vice President of Growth in managing the business development function and its teams, make sure the field completes the activity and reporting that our awards require, and use data to point the team at the referral sources that actually convert. Over time, this role may take on direct management of additional growth and business development functions.

What You Will Do

Lead the grant function

  • Serve as the internal authority on grants for executive, operational, clinical, and finance leadership.
  • Own a national pipeline and calendar, tracking funding opportunities in every state where we operate or intend to operate.
  • Pursue funding across federal discretionary awards, single state agency and block grant funding, state opioid response funding, opioid settlement dollars, county and municipal behavioral health funding, corporate giving, and private foundations.
  • Lead application development, including narrative, logic model, staffing plan, evaluation plan, and budget narrative.

Turn funding into growth

  • Build the grant strategy around our growth plan, targeting funding that supports market entry, new sites, new service lines, and expanded access.
  • Evaluate every opportunity on growth impact, resource requirement, match obligation, and probability of award, and bring leadership a clear recommendation to pursue or decline.
  • Report the portfolio in growth terms: dollars awarded, dollars under management, win rate, and the programs and access created.

Run awards cleanly

  • Keep every active award compliant, reported on time, and documented in an audit ready state.
  • Track spend-down with Finance and raise under-utilization or allowable-cost questions early enough to act on them.
  • Manage close-out, no-cost extensions, carryover requests, renewals, and competitive re-applications.
  • Train operational and business development staff on the grant functions required from the field, and oversee completion of that work.

Support business development and growth

  • Assist the Vice President of Growth in managing the business development function and its teams, including field priorities, territory coverage, and performance expectations.
  • Use conversion data, admission yield, payer mix, and level of care fit to direct field effort toward the referral sources that produce results.
  • Track activity, productivity, and return on investment in Salesforce, and maintain the dashboards that report it.

What We Are Looking For

  • Strong writing, financial, and analytical skills, and the presence to represent an organization with funders and senior external partners.

  • This is a rare combination of authorship and authority. You will not be handed a list of deadlines to service.   • Own the solution architecture for Genesys Cloud CX — defining how it's configured, integrated with our CRM, WFM, bots, and identity systems, and governed so complexity doesn't quietly accumulate over time.
  • Be the internal reviewer for every significant architectural decision made by our Systems Implementer and Managed Services Provider, validating that what gets built actually aligns with Chime's standards and long-term operating model.
  • Lead our most complex Genesys initiatives — from new AI platform integrations to major IVR redesigns — translating business and CX requirements into technically sound platform designs and keeping delivery tracks aligned across Engineering, SI, and MSP.

Content Marketing Manager

Full-Time (40 hours/week) | Fully Remote

Check out The Global Talent Co.’s talent network:

About the Company

The company builds an AI-driven platform for DevOps, enabling autonomous operations across cloud infrastructure, site reliability, and observability. The platform focuses on AI-powered SRE, infrastructure automation, and observability — helping engineering teams eliminate manual bottlenecks and operate at scale.

The company is scaling rapidly across product, market presence, and its sales team. This role is central to the pipeline engine that supports that growth.

The Role

Content is how the company reaches the engineers, SREs, platform teams, and technical leaders who need what we build. It drives discovery, shapes perception, and earns the attention of the people who decide we’re worth a closer look. As Content Marketing Manager, you own that content engine — from creation through to distribution — across every channel where our audience learns, searches, and forms opinions.

This role has two equally weighted halves:

  • Creating content that resonates with technical audiences — posts, articles, scripts, narratives, and short-form pieces that land because they’re written by someone who understands the world they’re written for.
  • Making sure that content travels — reaching the right people, in the right channels, at the velocity a fast-moving company needs.

To operate at that scale, this role owns the AI-powered workflow systems that turn a single piece of source material into channel-appropriate content across every surface where the company needs to show up. Building, running, and evolving those systems is a core part of the job — not an add-on.

You will work daily with our Product Marketing function, Technical Marketing Engineers, executive team, and engineering and product leadership across all three of our market segments. This is a senior individual contributor role — no direct reports, high ownership, high impact.

What You’ll Own

Content Creation

You originate, build on, and orchestrate all content the company puts into the market:

  • Original market-perspective content — pieces where the company has a point of view worth sharing (e.g. the shift toward agentic operations). This includes major owned research projects: our State of Reliability 2026 survey — analyzing over 50,000 incidents — is an example of the kind of project this role originates and owns end-to-end.
  • Channel-native content — LinkedIn posts, newsletter content, social threads, scripts, and short-form video that keep the company consistently present.
  • Content built on technical work — translating deep material from our Technical Marketing Engineers and positioning from Product Marketing into content that lands across channels and personas.
  • Executive thought leadership — turning the expertise of our CEO, CPO, and engineering leadership into a consistent, credible external presence.
  • Editorial standards — establishing and maintaining voice, tone, and quality bar for everything published under the the company brand.

Distribution Across Channels

You make sure the company content reaches the right people, wherever they spend time:

  • Social platforms — LinkedIn as the primary surface for company and individual presence, plus other networks where DevOps and SRE practitioners gather.
  • Engineering communities — Discords, Slacks, Reddit, Hacker News, CNCF forums, and other practitioner spaces, with content that earns credibility rather than imposes on it.
  • Video platforms — YouTube and other channels where our audience learns and evaluates.
  • Owned channels — the the company website, email and newsletter programs, and resource and video library.
  • Earned media and guest contributions — supporting placements in publications our buyers actually read, and coordinating opportunities for the company team members to contribute.
  • Search and AI discovery — working with the broader marketing team to ensure content is structured for both SEO and AEO (AI Engine Optimisation), so it surfaces in traditional and AI-assisted discovery.

AI-Powered Workflow Systems

Operating across this many channels at velocity is only possible with serious AI leverage. You’ll own the workflow systems that make it work:

  • Building and evolving AI-assisted content workflows that turn source material into channel-appropriate output at scale, with human-in-the-loop quality control.
  • Designing systems and skill-based prompts that produce consistent voice and quality across formats.
  • Continuously improving the workflow stack as the team grows and AI tooling evolves.
  • Acting as the in-house standard-setter for what good AI-augmented content production looks like.

Amplification of the company’s People

the company’s engineers, product team, and leaders are doing work worth talking about. You make sure it travels:

  • Coaching and supporting team members on building consistent external voices, particularly on LinkedIn.
  • Helping engineering and product translate what they’re building into stories that resonate externally.
  • Identifying and building relationships with credible external voices in the DevOps, SRE, and cloud-native space — for joint posts, podcast appearances, and community presence.

Contributing Across the Marketing System

  • Demand generation — supplying content that powers paid, outbound, and lifecycle programs; feeding performance data back into what you create next.
  • Events — pre-event, at-event, and post-event content that extends the reach of field activity.
  • Analytics — tracking content performance across channels and using that data to direct effort.

What We’re Looking For

  • Ecosystem fluency in the DevOps, SRE, or platform engineering world — you know the audiences, the conversations, and what credibility looks like in these communities. In practice: you understand concepts like DORA metrics, the platform engineering vs. SRE debate, or how teams think about observability and incident management. You don’t need to have been an engineer; we have Technical Marketing Engineers for deep technical expertise. What we need is the ability to engage with that world on its own terms.
  • A strong content instinct — you can tell what will resonate with a technical audience and what won’t, and you can produce content that lands rather than content that just exists.
  • Multi-channel distribution craft — you understand how content behaves differently on LinkedIn vs. in a community vs. on a blog vs. in email, and you can make the same source material work across all of them.
  • Genuine AI fluency at the workflow level — you build and operate AI-assisted systems, not just use AI tools occasionally. You’re comfortable owning a workflow stack that produces content across many formats and channels at velocity.
  • Hands-on fluency across modern content marketing tools — our current stack includes HubSpot, Google Analytics, Google Search Console, Canva, Claude, ChatGPT, Perplexity, and AirOps. We expect comfort across this kind of toolset and active engagement in evolving it as the space changes.
  • A reach orientation — you think about where the right people are, what they pay attention to, and what the company needs to do to show up there credibly and consistently.
  • A bias toward data — you track what’s landing, adjust based on signal, and make the case for content investment with evidence.

Comfort operating at high velocity across many channels and personas — from individual contributors (platform engineers, SREs, DevOps engineers) up to senior technical leaders (VPs of Engineering, CTOs).

At The Global Talent Co., our mission is to bridge the gap between leading global tech companies and amazing global talent. We believe everyone deserves equal access to opportunities, regardless of the country they are born in.

Life at BMS

At RayzeBio, every day is an opportunity to ignite meaningful change. As a wholly-owned subsidiary of Bristol Myers Squibb, RayzeBio blends the nimble, pioneering spirit of an emergent biotech with the global expertise and resources of a leading innovator in oncology. Our mission is to develop transformative radiopharmaceutical therapies that offer new hope for patients living with cancer. Here, you’ll join a multidisciplinary team where your ideas are valued, your expertise is amplified, and collaboration is at the heart of everything we do. From day one, expect to make an immediate impact—on our science, on our teams, and most importantly, on patients. Learn more about RayzeBio:


The Senior Medical Director, Radiopharmaceutical Imaging (RPI) provides strategic and operational leadership for the development of RayzeBio’s diagnostic imaging pipeline across disease areas, including but not limited to prostate cancer, hepatocellular cancer, and neuroendocrine tumors. This role is accountable for the imaging portfolio strategy, development plans, and key decision making from IND-enabling activities through Phase 0–Phase 3 clinical trials, including medical monitoring and benefit-risk assessments. The Senior Medical Director partners closely with cross-functional leaders (Clinical Development, Translational, Regulatory, Biomarkers, Safety, CMC, Biostatistics, Clinical Operations, Medical Affairs, and Commercial) to ensure integrated, high-quality execution, clear governance, and timely delivery of program milestones aligned with patient needs and RayzeBio’s business objectives.

Job Responsibilities

Essential duties and responsibilities include the following. Other duties may be assigned.

  • Define and own the diagnostic imaging portfolio strategy and target product profiles for nominated candidates, incorporating competitive intelligence and evolving standards of care.

  • Serve as imaging Clinical Development lead, providing medical and scientific direction across programs and ensuring robust, decision-oriented development plans.

  • Lead and influence cross-functional matrix teams and external partners (investigators, academic collaborators, CROs, central readers) to design and execute early- and late-phase imaging studies.

  • Accountable for protocol concepts and critical document content, including protocols, investigator brochures, SAP inputs, clinical study reports, and key regulatory and medical communications. Performsmedical monitoring and data review activities in support of clinical studies

  • Provide medical oversight for trial conduct, including eligibility/risk assessments, safety review, medical monitoring strategy, and escalation pathways in collaboration with Drug Safety/Pharmacovigilance.

  • Lead governance for imaging programs, including data review activities and Independent Data Monitoring Committees (IDMCs)/Data Monitoring Committees (DMCs) as applicable.

  • Translate findings from research, translational, and nonclinical studies into imaging development opportunities and decision points; synthesize evidence to drive go/no-go recommendations.

  • Drive strategic regulatory engagement as clinical lead for health authority interactions, including briefing package strategy, participation in meetings, and representation of clinical rationale.

  • Establish and maintain strong relationships with clinical investigators and key opinion leaders; represent RayzeBio externally at scientific meetings and advisory boards as needed.

  • Work closely with CROs and vendors in the execution of clinical trials for radiopharmaceutical imaging agents

  • Participate in health authority interactions, preparation of briefing books, HA requests for information and regulatory filings.

  • Partner with Medical Affairs and Commercial to develop the evidence-generation strategy and lifecycle plans for radiopharmaceutical imaging within the broader RayzeBio portfolio.

  • Contribute to resource planning, timeline and budget management, risk mitigation/contingency planning, and vendor oversight to ensure delivery against milestones.

  • Leverages AI to drive program, portfolio, or functional performance through prioritization and scaled adoption.

  • Willing to travel approximately 30% of the time. Evening and weekend work may be required.

Education and Experience

  • MD (or equivalent) with 8+ years of pharmaceutical/biotech and/or relevant academic clinical experience, including substantial experience in oncology diagnostic development and/or radiopharmaceutical imaging agent development through regulatory submissions

  • Demonstrated leadership in clinical development with increasing levels of responsibility, including leading cross-functional teams and driving strategy through key development decisions.

  • Experience across early- and late-phase protocol development and execution, including study start-up, oversight of conduct, analysis inputs, and reporting.

  • Proven experience working closely with investigative sites (PIs, sub-investigators, coordinators) and managing external vendors (e.g., CROs, imaging core labs).

Skills and Qualifications

  • Patient-focused with deep commitment to improving outcomes for people with cancer and passion for developing novel radiopharmaceuticals and imaging agents.

  • Strategic clinical development leader who can set direction, align stakeholders, and drive decisions in a fast-paced, high-accountability environment.

  • Demonstrated ability to lead through influence in a matrix organization; able to build alignment across functions and levels, including senior leadership.

  • Strong scientific judgment and benefit–risk mindset; able to interpret complex imaging and clinical data and translate insights into clear development recommendations.

  • Executive-level written and verbal communication skills, including compelling presentations and the ability to represent the program effectively with health authorities and external experts.

  • Experience across early- and late-phase protocol development and execution, including study start-up, oversight of conduct, analysis inputs, and reporting.

  • Strong understanding of radiopharmaceutical imaging agent development, central reading paradigms, imaging endpoints, and operational considerations for multicenter trials.

  • Proven experience working closely with investigative sites (PIs, sub-investigators, coordinators) and managing external vendors (e.g., CROs, imaging core labs).

  • Ability to function in a highly regulated environment and to adhere to RayzeBio guidelines and standard operating procedures (SOPs).

  • Solid understanding of GCP and ICH guidelines.

Physical Demands

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit, reach with hands and arms, and talk or hear. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 20 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision and distance vision.

Work Environment

The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

jobs.description:
Position:Chief Financial Officer (CFO)

About the Role

We are seeking an accomplished and commercially strategic Chief Financial Officer (CFO) to lead the financial strategy, financial performance, capital management, investment finance, treasury, reporting, and financial governance of a diversified Insurance & Investment organization.

The CFO will serve as a key member of the executive leadership team and strategic advisor to the CEO/President and Board, providing leadership across financial planning, insurance accounting, capital and solvency management, investment portfolio performance, asset-liability management, treasury, risk, regulatory reporting, and corporate development.

The successful candidate will combine deep financial expertise with strong commercial and investment acumen and will be capable of operating in a highly regulated financial-services environment.

Key Responsibilities

1. Financial Strategy & Executive Leadership

Develop and execute the organization's overall financial strategy.

Advise the CEO, President, and Board on financial performance, capital allocation, investment strategy, and enterprise value creation.

Translate corporate strategy into financial plans, budgets, forecasts, and measurable objectives.

Lead financial decision-making across insurance, investment, and corporate operations.

Establish strong financial governance and accountability across the organization.

2. Financial Planning, Budgeting & Performance

Lead annual budgeting, forecasting, and long-term financial planning.

Develop financial models and scenario analyses to support strategic decisions.

Monitor revenue, profitability, expenses, capital efficiency, and operating performance.

Establish financial KPIs and executive dashboards.

Identify opportunities to improve profitability, efficiency, and shareholder returns.

3. Insurance Finance & Performance

Oversee financial management of insurance operations, including premiums, claims, reserves, expenses, and underwriting performance.

Monitor key insurance financial metrics including loss ratios, combined ratios, expense ratios, and underwriting profitability.

Partner with actuarial, underwriting, claims, and risk teams to assess financial performance and emerging exposures.

Ensure appropriate financial treatment and reporting of insurance liabilities and reserves.

Support pricing, product profitability, reinsurance, and portfolio decisions from a financial perspective.

4. Investment Finance & Portfolio Management

Provide financial oversight of the organization's investment portfolio and investment activities.

Partner with the CIO/Chief Investment Officer and Investment Committee on portfolio strategy and performance.

Monitor investment income, realized/unrealized gains, asset allocation, liquidity, and risk-adjusted returns.

Evaluate investment opportunities and strategic asset-allocation decisions.

Ensure investment activities are aligned with the organization's liabilities, liquidity requirements, risk appetite, and regulatory requirements.

5. Capital, Solvency & Balance Sheet Management

Lead capital planning and balance-sheet optimization.

Monitor solvency, capital adequacy, liquidity, leverage, and financial resilience.

Develop strategies to optimize the organization's capital structure and return on capital.

Assess the financial impact of major business, investment, and insurance decisions on capital requirements.

Work closely with Risk and Actuarial functions on capital and solvency assessments.

6. Asset-Liability Management (ALM)

Provide executive financial oversight of asset-liability management.

Ensure investment portfolios are appropriately aligned with insurance liabilities and liquidity requirements.

Monitor duration, interest-rate sensitivity, liquidity gaps, and market exposures.

Support development of ALM strategies and balance-sheet optimization initiatives.

Ensure appropriate financial stress testing and scenario analysis.

7. Treasury & Liquidity

Oversee treasury, cash management, liquidity planning, and banking relationships.

Maintain adequate liquidity to meet claims, operating obligations, investment commitments, and strategic requirements.

Optimize cash deployment and short-term investment strategies.

Monitor interest-rate, foreign-exchange, credit, and liquidity exposures.

Establish robust treasury policies and controls.

8. Regulatory & Financial Reporting

Ensure accurate, timely, and transparent financial reporting to the Board, shareholders, regulators, and other stakeholders.

Oversee statutory accounts, management reporting, regulatory returns, and consolidated financial statements.

Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards and insurance regulations.

Lead relationships with external auditors, regulators, actuarial advisers, tax advisers, and other professional stakeholders.

Maintain strong financial controls and governance frameworks.

9. Risk Management & Financial Controls

Establish effective financial risk-management frameworks.

Monitor exposure to market, credit, liquidity, underwriting, operational, interest-rate, and foreign-exchange risks.

Strengthen internal controls, financial policies, and governance processes.

Work closely with the CRO, Chief Actuary, CIO, and other executives to manage enterprise-wide financial risks.

Ensure appropriate stress testing and contingency planning.

10. Reinsurance & Capital Optimization

Provide financial oversight of reinsurance strategy and economics.

Evaluate the financial and capital implications of reinsurance arrangements.

Monitor reinsurance recoverables, counterparty exposure, and profitability.

Support optimization of risk transfer, capital efficiency, and balance-sheet resilience.

11. Corporate Development & Strategic Investments

Lead financial evaluation of acquisitions, strategic investments, joint ventures, and business expansion opportunities.

Oversee financial due diligence, valuation, transaction modeling, and investment cases.

Assess potential M&A opportunities and their impact on capital, solvency, earnings, and shareholder value.

Support negotiations with investors, financial institutions, and strategic partners.

12. Investor & Stakeholder Relations

Develop strong relationships with shareholders, institutional investors, banks, rating agencies, regulators, and other financial stakeholders.

Communicate financial performance, capital strategy, investment results, and business outlook to key stakeholders.

Support investor presentations, Board materials, and strategic financial communications.

13. Finance Transformation & Technology

Modernize finance systems, reporting infrastructure, ERP platforms, and financial analytics.

Improve automation, data quality, forecasting, and management reporting.

Establish real-time visibility into financial, insurance, investment, and risk performance.

Drive continuous improvement within the finance function.

14. Leadership & Talent Development

Lead Finance, FP&A, Treasury, Accounting, Financial Reporting, Tax, and related functions.

Build a high-performing and commercially focused finance organization.

Develop finance leadership talent and succession plans.

Promote a culture of integrity, accountability, financial discipline, and business partnership.

Key Performance Indicators

The CFO will be accountable for:

Revenue and earnings growth

Operating and net profitability

Return on equity (ROE)

Return on capital

Capital adequacy and solvency

Investment portfolio performance

Investment income and risk-adjusted returns

Combined ratio / underwriting profitability

Expense efficiency

Liquidity and cash-flow management

Balance-sheet optimization

Budget and forecast accuracy

Regulatory and financial reporting quality

Cost of capital

Financial risk management

Shareholder value creation

Candidate Profile

Essential Experience

15+ years of progressive finance experience, including significant executive leadership.

Previous experience as CFO, Group CFO, Finance Director, VP Finance, Deputy CFO, or equivalent.

Significant experience within insurance, asset management, investment management, banking, pensions, financial services, or a related regulated financial institution.

Strong understanding of insurance financial statements, investment portfolios, capital management, and regulatory requirements.

Proven experience managing complex balance sheets, liquidity, capital, and financial performance.

Strong experience working with Boards, regulators, auditors, investors, rating agencies, and senior executives.

Demonstrated experience in financial strategy, investment analysis, and capital allocation.

Preferred Experience

Experience as Group CFO within a diversified insurance or financial-services group.

Experience across both insurance and investment/asset-management businesses.

Experience with life insurance, general insurance, health insurance, pensions, or reinsurance.

Exposure to institutional investment portfolios and alternative investments.

Experience with M&A, strategic investments, capital raising, restructuring, or corporate transformation.

Experience operating across multiple jurisdictions or regulated markets.

Experience interacting with insurance regulators and rating agencies.

Education & Professional Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Business Administration, or a related discipline.

Professional qualification such as CA, ACCA, CPA, CMA, CFA, or equivalent strongly preferred.

MBA or Master's degree in Finance/Business is an advantage.

Relevant insurance, actuarial, investment, or risk-management qualifications are advantageous.

Core Competencies

Insurance Finance

Corporate Finance

Investment Finance

Capital & Solvency Management

Asset-Liability Management

Treasury & Liquidity

Financial Planning & Analysis

Investment Analysis

Financial Modeling

Risk Management

Regulatory Reporting

Insurance Accounting

M&A & Corporate Development

Capital Allocation

Investor Relations

Corporate Governance

Financial Transformation

Leadership Characteristics

The successful CFO will be:

Strategic, commercially minded, and financially rigorous

Highly analytical and investment-oriented

Experienced in highly regulated environments

Strong in capital and balance-sheet management

Comfortable engaging with Boards, regulators, investors, and rating agencies

Able to balance growth, profitability, liquidity, capital, and risk

An effective strategic partner to the CEO, CIO, CRO, and Chief Actuary

Strong in complex financial decision-making

A transformational finance leader capable of building high-performing teams

Compensation

A competitive executive compensation package comprising base salary, performance-based incentives, executive benefits, and other benefits commensurate with experience and market benchmarks.

Machinify is a leading healthcare intelligence company with expertise across the payment continuum, delivering unmatched value, transparency, and efficiency to health plan clients across the country. We’re constantly reimagining what’s possible in our industry, creating disruptively simple, powerfully clear ways to maximize financial outcomes and drive down healthcare costs.

The Coding Validation Specialist (CVS), Behavioral Health / Substance Use Disorder reviews provider medical records to validate the accuracy of outpatient facility and professional behavioral health and substance use disorder (SUD) claims. This role requires specialized knowledge of psychiatric, psychotherapy, and SUD treatment coding, including DSM-5-based diagnosis coding, H-codes, and applicable CPT and HCPCS Level II codes, to ensure the accuracy of coding, billing, and documentation. The CVS reports findings, communicates results, ensures compliance with regulatory, payer, and client requirements, and maintains quality and productivity standards. This role may be filled by a licensed nurse (RN or LPN/LVN) with coding experience, or by a certified medical coder with behavioral health/SUD specialization.

What You’ll Do:

  • Performs comprehensive analysis and review of claim information and associated medical records to validate that billed procedure and service codes are accurate and support the payment for behavioral health and/or SUD services.
  • Maintains expert knowledge of CPT and HCPCS Level II coding conventions and rules specific to behavioral health and SUD services, including psychiatric evaluation and management, psychotherapy, medication-assisted treatment (MAT), opioid treatment program (OTP) services, intensive outpatient (IOP) and partial hospitalization (PHP) levels of care, and applied behavior analysis (ABA), as well as Official Coding Guidelines, AMA Coding Clinic, and DSM-5/ICD-10-CM diagnosis coding, remaining current on changes to coding guidelines, industry trends, and best practices.
  • Analyzes, reviews, and resolves coding issues related to reimbursement, compliance, and client-specific policies for behavioral health and SUD claims.
  • Validates patient data by comparing claims data received with patient medical records, including treatment plans, progress notes, and level-of-care documentation specific to behavioral health and SUD services.
  • Develops and applies the appropriate rationale for any coding change affecting the APC or EAPG assignment, citing supporting references such as Official Coding Guidelines, AMA Coding guidelines, Medicare or Medicaid Billing Manuals, ASAM criteria where applicable, and coding conventions.
  • Analyzes claim and supporting documentation for all claim characteristics impacting reimbursement, including revenue code and CPT/HCPCS code pairing (for example, psychiatric and chemical dependency intensive outpatient revenue codes paired with corresponding procedure codes).
  • Maintains accuracy, quality, and production standards relating to the identification of incorrect coding, assignment of correct codes, and documentation of review outcomes.
  • Applies working knowledge of 42 CFR Part 2 confidentiality requirements and mental health parity (MHPAEA) considerations when handling and documenting behavioral health and SUD record review.
  • Uses computer applications, Grouper/Pricer software, ICD-10-CM encoder software, and Microsoft Office products.
  • Abides by the Standards of Ethical Coding as set forth by the American Health Information Management Association.

What You Bring:

  • High School Diploma or equivalent GED.
  • One of the following: (a) active, unrestricted nursing license (RN or LPN/LVN) in good standing, or (b) national coding certification as Registered Health Information Administrator (RHIA), Registered Health Information Technician (RHIT), Certified Professional Coder (CPC), or Certified Coding Specialist (CCS).
  • Minimum of three years of experience in coding or auditing behavioral health and/or SUD claims.
  • Working knowledge of DSM-5 diagnostic coding as applied to ICD-10-CM, and of behavioral health/SUD documentation requirements including treatment plans, progress notes, and authorization standards.
  • Comprehensive knowledge of the APC structure and regulatory requirements applicable to behavioral health and SUD services.
  • Comfort with AI-powered search tools and a growth mindset toward learning new technologies

jobs.excerpt: The Aspen Group (TAG) is one of the largest and most trusted retail healthcare business support organizations in the U.
jobs.description:
The Aspen Group (TAG) is one of the largest and most trusted retail healthcare business support organizations in the U.S., supporting over 23,000 healthcare professionals and team members at more than 1,150 locations across 48 states. Our five supported healthcare practices operate under the brands Aspen Dental, ClearChoice, WellNow, Chapter Aesthetic Studio, and Lovet. We’re committed to enabling healthcare professionals to focus on patient care while we handle the business operations that support them.

We are seeking an Infrastructure Systems Architect to own architectural oversight of the systems that manage, monitor, and secure a device ecosystem of approximately 50,000 endpoints supporting 20,000+ users across 1,500+ locations for a large dental services organization (DSO) and affiliated medical services businesses. This is a senior individual contributor role that is equal parts architecture and hands-on engineering: the successful candidate will help define the target-state design for fleet management, telemetry, and automation platforms, and then help build the integrations, services, and tooling that make that design real.

The majority of the scope centers on enterprise endpoint management and monitoring at scale. The role also extends to the platforms and workstations that run clinical applications and connected clinical devices, including digital X-ray, CBCT imaging, and intraoral 3D scanning systems. The ideal candidate has built and supported scalable, enterprise-grade device fleet management and observability systems, writes production-quality code, and has led large-scale device deployment and integration programs.

This role provides architectural oversight and advanced technical support to the Endpoint Engineering, Field Support, Implementation, Network and Imaging Modality teams, and serves as the final technical authority for fleet management systems design.

Key Responsibilities:

Architecture & Strategy

  • Champion the effort to define the target-state architecture, standards, design patterns, and roadmap for endpoint management, telemetry, inventory, patching, and remote support platforms.
  • Establish architectural governance: design review processes, architecture decision records, non-functional requirements, and exception handling.
  • Evaluate current state commercial endpoint management, RMM, and observability platforms to identify gaps and opportunities to upgrade or augment functionality with custom tooling. Lead proof-of-concept work and build-vs-buy analyses with TCO and operational-burden reasoning.
  • Design for scale and resilience: multi-tenant/multi-brand separation, safe and effective rollouts.
  • Partner with Security and Infrastructure leadership to align fleet architecture with Zero Trust principles, conditional access, device compliance posture, and least-privilege models.
  • Produce and maintain authoritative documentation: architecture diagrams, data flows, integration contracts, runbooks, and roadmaps.

Hands-On Engineering & Development

  • Design and build the tooling, APIs, connectors, and automation frameworks that integrate endpoint management platforms with ITSM, CMDB, identity, asset, and location data systems of record.
  • Write production-quality code in .NET, Go, Python, and JavaScript/TypeScript for agents, microservices, orchestration jobs, and internal tooling.
  • Collaborate with observability team to help build device telemetry and observability that provide accurate real-time fleet health, compliance, and inventory reporting.
  • Develop self-healing and remediation automations that detect and corrects failed policy or application deployments and configuration non-compliance without human intervention.
  • Implement CI/CD, infrastructure-as-code, testing, and release management practices for all fleet management tooling and configuration artifacts.
  • Prototype and harden new capabilities before transitioning them to the Endpoint Engineering and Operations teams for day-to-day ownership.

Deployment & Integration Programs

  • Lead the implementation of best practices for fleetwide safe and effective application deployments.
  • Provide architectural oversight for large-scale device deployment, refresh, migration, and DeNovo/acquisition integration programs.
  • Help design zero-touch provisioning, imaging, and enrollment workflows that allow field and third-party technicians to deploy devices consistently with minimal specialized skill.
  • Define the technical integration playbook for acquired practices and new-build locations, including device onboarding, standards conformance, and remediation of non-standard estates.

Clinical Systems Scope

  • Extend fleet management, monitoring, and patching standards to workstations and appliances that host clinical applications and connected clinical devices, including digital X-ray, CBCT, and intraoral 3D scanning systems.
  • Design management approaches for constrained or vendor-controlled clinical endpoints, balancing security and patch currency against vendor support requirements and clinical uptime.
  • Ensure fleet management designs support HIPAA safeguards and appropriate handling of systems that touch protected health information.

Leadership & Advanced Support

  • Serve as the final escalation point for complex, cross-domain technical issues involving application deployments, device management, telemetry, and integration systems.
  • Mentor Principal, Senior, and mid-level engineers in system design, software engineering practice, automation, and documentation rigor.
  • Participate in cross-functional design and readiness reviews ensuring solutions meet enterprise SLAs, security requirements, and supportability standards.
  • Translate technical direction into clear recommendations and trade-offs for leadership teams.

Skills & Qualifications:

Education:Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field (or equivalent work experience).

Experience:10+ years in systems architecture, platform engineering, or software engineering roles, including significant experience designing and operating device fleet management and monitoring systems at enterprise scale (10,000+ devices; 50,000+ preferred) across a highly distributed, multi-site footprint.

Technical Skills

  • Experience with endpoint agent architecture and lifecycle: deployment, versioning, health monitoring, and safe rollback across a large fleet.
  • Strong, current application development experience with production code in one or more major programming languages or frameworks (.NET/C#, Go, Python, and JavaScript/TypeScript).
  • Proven design and delivery of distributed, service-oriented systems: REST/gRPC APIs, message queues and event-driven patterns, relational and time-series data stores, caching, and secure secrets management.
  • Familiarity with commercial endpoint management platforms — Microsoft Intune, Autopilot, MECM/SCCM, and JAMF.
  • Monitoring and observability tooling and practice (e.g., Grafana, Prometheus or equivalent), including metrics, logging, alerting design, and alert-fatigue management.
  • Cloud platform experience (Azure & GCP preferred; AWS acceptable), containerization, and infrastructure-as-code (Terraform or equivalent).
  • Solid grasp of endpoint security fundamentals: EDR, disk encryption, patch and vulnerability management, hardening baselines, and compliance reporting.
  • Windows and macOS internals, plus mobile and purpose-built/appliance device management; scripting in PowerShell.
  • Networking fluency sufficient to design across a distributed branch estate: DNS, DHCP, TCP/IP, VPN, SD-WAN, proxy/firewall traversal, and bandwidth-constrained site behavior.
  • Data modeling and reporting for asset, inventory, and compliance data, with an emphasis on a single trusted source of fleet truth.

Soft Skills

  • Strong analytical and systems-thinking ability, with the judgment to choose simple, supportable designs over complex ones.
  • Excellent written communication and documentation rigor; able to produce architecture artifacts that engineers can build from without further interpretation.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence without authority and align engineering, security, operations, and business stakeholders around a shared technical direction.
  • Self-directed ownership: identifies gaps proactively, drives them to resolution.
  • Mentorship and technical leadership capability across engineering levels.
  • Comfort operating in a fast-paced environment with multiple concurrent and competing priorities.

Additional Qualifications (Preferred):

  • Experience in healthcare, dental, retail, restaurant, or another highly distributed multi-site industry.
  • Experience integrating device management platforms with ITSM/CMDB tooling (e.g., ServiceNow) and asset lifecycle systems.
  • Experience with merger, acquisition, or de novo location IT integration at scale.
  • Exposure to AI/ML-assisted operations — anomaly detection, predictive hardware failure, or automated triage of endpoint telemetry.

Working Conditions:

Hours:Full-time. Occasional after-hours or weekend work to support major deployments, migrations, and critical escalations.

Location: Syracuse NY; Chicago IL or Remote

Travel:Occasional travel (less than 10%) to corporate offices, staging facilities, and field locations.

Reporting:Individual contributor role providing architectural direction to the Endpoint Engineering, Implementation, and Field Support teams; no direct reports to start with possibility of having one or two reports.

*A generous benefits package that includes paid time off, health, dental, vision, and 401(k) savings plan with match

*Salary: $115,000-175,000/year

Les tâches ne sont généralement pas routinières et peuvent nécessiter l’exercice du jugement à l’intérieur de paramètres et de procédures opérationnelles générales. Les problèmes rencontrés sont de nature générale et peuvent nécessiter une certaine analyse afin d’être résolus.

**To be eligible for this position, you must reside in the same country/sales region where the job is located. **

Location: Canada, Home-Based

May also include feasibility or maintenance activities.

Review documents for completeness, consistency and accuracy, under guidance of senior staff.
