Toptal is a global network of top talent in business, design, and technology that enables companies to scale their teams, on-demand. With $200+ million in annual revenue and team members based around the globe, Toptal is the world’s largest fully remote workforce.

We take the best elements of virtual teams and combine them with a support structure that encourages innovation, social interaction, and fun. We see no borders, move at a fast pace, and are never afraid to break the mold.

Job Summary:

Want to make an impact by innovating how top global companies build teams and adapt to the Future of Work? As an Account Executive, you’ll be responsible for driving growth by acquiring new clients, re-engaging former clients, and expanding existing high-value accounts to maximize long-term growth opportunities. Success in this role comes from your ability to strategically identify and engage potential clients, uncover their key business challenges, and align Toptal’s solutions to meet their needs. This is a full-cycle sales role, which means you will take full ownership of your pipeline, including targeting ideal clients, setting your own high-quality meetings, and driving the sales process through to close.

This is a remote position. We do not offer visa sponsorship or assistance. Applicants must be authorized to work in the US at the time of hire. Resumes and communication must be submitted in English.

Responsibilities:

The following information is intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or required skills.

  • Drive full-cycle sales by identifying and engaging high-potential prospects, re-engaging dormant clients, and generating new opportunities through strategic outreach.
  • Conduct outbound prospecting via phone, email, and LinkedIn to identify opportunities, present Toptal’s value proposition, and secure new business.
  • Effectively manage the sales funnel to optimize lead progression, coordinate communication among various stakeholders, and diligently follow up on accounts to nurture leads toward conversion.
  • Ensure timely and accurate CRM documentation, while providing leadership with clear sales forecasts and pipeline insights.
  • As you become more comfortable in the role, contribute to evolving our demand generation strategy and tactics to expand pipeline growth and market reach.

In the first week, expect to:

  • Onboard and integrate into Toptal.
  • Learn Toptal’s model, our value proposition, and our story.
  • Work with cross-functional teams to understand how you can utilize our incredible global team to build client relationships and drive success.
  • Learn the breadth of Toptal’s impact on the world’s largest companies.
  • Grasp the importance of the outbound function to the success of growing Toptal.
  • Understand our sales method and our selling process to set you up for success.

In the first month, expect to:

  • Complete our personalized sales training program, complete with mock calls, cold calls, and role-play scenarios.
  • Learn how to use outreach tools (SalesLoft, Zoominfo, SalesNavigator).
  • Learn the process for outreach, including calling, emailing, and LinkedIn messaging. Implement an outreach process and hit 1-month objectives.
  • Learn how to analyze industry drivers, business problems, and target buyers.

In the first three months, expect to:

  • Uncover new opportunities with existing accounts and target accounts that result in revenue-generating engagements for Toptal.
  • Hit call/email quotas and fully ramped objectives.
  • Become proficient in using our SaaS tools.
  • Learn how to maintain excellent data integrity in Salesforce.com.

In the first six months, expect to:

  • Continuously hit fully ramped quotas and objectives.
  • Assist with training and onboarding new Account Executives.
  • Build new and existing client relationships, expand Toptal’s partnership with new and existing clients.
  • Suggest, implement and experiment with new lead and demand generation activities.

In the first year, expect to:

  • Have closed multiple net new accounts from the strategic account list, while exercising discretion and independent judgment.
  • Become a mentor to new members of the team, helping them learn about Toptal, our model, and how proper business development practices can improve relationships and increase revenue.
  • Consistently maintain a high level of success by meeting and exceeding 100% of monthly and quarterly key performance indicators and targets.
  • Establish a career path for advancement.

Qualifications and Job Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree is required.
  • Minimum 2 years sales experience, including at least 1 year in a closing role.
  • Experience in B2B or SaaS sales is strongly preferred.
  • Proven success in full-cycle sales, including lead generation, prospecting, running virtual sales calls, funnel management, and closing.
  • Proficient with sales tools such as Salesforce, Salesloft, and LinkedIn Sales Navigator, with a demonstrated ability to quickly learn new technologies and adapt to evolving sales platforms.
  • Outstanding written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, rapidly growing company and handle a wide variety of challenges, deadlines, and a diverse array of contacts.
  • You’re persistent in the face of setbacks, eager to understand people and problems, and motivated to go above and beyond to reach your goals.
  • You thrive with autonomy and ownership. We’re looking for someone who can be held accountable for leading their portion of the business.
  • You must be a world-class individual contributor to thrive at Toptal. You will not be here just to tell other people what to do.

Essential Job Functions

  • Regularly and reliably attend scheduled virtual team meetings on camera.
  • Work independently with minimal supervision.
  • Use all required digital collaboration tools.
  • Prioritize and self-manage workflows and deadlines.

US FLSA Classification: Full-Time/Exempt

This position receives a base salary and is also eligible to earn monthly commissions based on revenue generated from engagements sold. For candidates who meet the qualifications and job requirements listed above, Individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

jobs.title: Engineering Manager - Virtual Appliance Platform
jobs.excerpt: About SailPoint SailPoint is the leader in identity security for the cloud enterprise.
jobs.description:
About SailPoint

SailPoint is the leader in identity security for the cloud enterprise. Our identity security solutions secure and enable thousands of companies worldwide, giving our customers unmatched visibility across their digital workforce and helping ensure that workers have the right access to do their jobs—no more, no less.

Built on a foundation of AI and machine learning, SailPoint Identity Security delivers the right level of access to the right identities and resources at the right time, matching the scale, velocity, and changing needs of today’s cloud-oriented modern enterprise.

About the Role

As an Engineering Manager, you will lead and grow the software engineering team responsible for a critical virtual appliance that customers deploy within their private environments. The appliance provides a secure, reliable connection between customer-managed systems and SailPoint Identity Security. You will own engineering execution, collaborate with Product Management on the roadmap, and help the team deliver meaningful customer outcomes with greater speed and predictability.

In a typical day, you may coach an engineer, review an architectural proposal, refine sprint priorities, coordinate a release or incident follow-up with a peer team, and communicate roadmap progress and risks. You will not be expected to write code routinely, but you will be technically engaged: able to read code, understand the systems your team owns, ask insightful questions, and guide sound decisions involving Linux, virtualization, containerization, and customer-deployed software.

You will continue developing the team’s Scrum practices around a predictable two-week sprint cadence while preserving the flexibility to respond to urgent customer and operational needs. You will also champion responsible use of modern AI and LLM capabilities to improve engineering effectiveness, quality, decision-making, and business outcomes.

This role is based in India. Candidates may work remotely, in a hybrid arrangement, or from SailPoint’s Pune office. Substantial daily overlap with U.S. working hours is required. Periodic team gatherings in the United States provide optional opportunities for in-person collaboration and travel.


About the Team

This distributed software engineering team owns the complete lifecycle of SailPoint’s customer-deployed virtual appliance—from architecture and development through distribution, installation, upgrades, patching, compatibility, vulnerability remediation, diagnostics, reliability, and incident response. Engineers participate in an on-call rotation for customer-impacting issues.

The team works closely with Product Management and with experts across security, vulnerability management, architecture, release engineering, support, and other engineering organizations. It is strengthening the platform’s foundations while pursuing an ambitious roadmap designed to make the appliance easier for customers to deploy, operate, and rely on.

Roadmap for Success

The following milestones describe how success in this role will be measured. Specific delivery and reliability targets will be established using current platform and team baselines.


30 days

  • Build trusted working relationships with every team member and key partners across Product Management, architecture, security, vulnerability management, release engineering, and support.
  • Develop a working understanding of the platform architecture, codebase, roadmap, release lifecycle, customer experience, operational history, and major technical risks.
  • Assess the team’s current delivery practices, staffing needs, and near-term priorities, then share a focused 90-day action plan with stakeholders.


90 days

  • Take full ownership of engineering execution, team development, delivery reporting, dependency management, and risk communication.
  • Establish a consistent two-week Scrum cadence with clear backlog refinement, sprint planning, reviews, retrospectives, and visible progress against commitments.
  • Agree with Product Management and technical partners on a prioritized stabilization plan, roadmap sequencing, and baseline measures for delivery predictability and platform reliability.
  • Define and begin executing a hiring and team-development plan aligned with the roadmap.


6 months

  • Demonstrate measurable improvement against the delivery and reliability baselines established during the first 90 days.
  • Deliver the highest-priority platform stabilization work while maintaining visible progress on customer-focused roadmap commitments.
  • Strengthen production ownership through effective incident response, learning reviews, vulnerability remediation, and follow-through on reliability improvements.
  • Introduce practical, responsible AI-assisted workflows that produce demonstrable improvements in engineering quality, decision-making, or delivery efficiency.
  • Make measurable progress against the agreed hiring plan and ensure every engineer has clear expectations, feedback, and development goals.


1 year

  • Meet the platform stability, supportability, and delivery targets agreed with engineering and product stakeholders.
  • Operate a mature, predictable Scrum model that consistently balances roadmap delivery with customer and operational priorities.
  • Deliver meaningful roadmap milestones that improve how customers deploy, upgrade, operate, and rely on the virtual appliance.
  • Establish and begin executing a multi-quarter technical strategy for the platform’s continued modernization and architectural evolution.
  • Build a stronger, appropriately staffed team with clear ownership, healthy collaboration, and demonstrated growth in both people and technical capability.


Requirements

  • 8+ years of professional software engineering experience, including 5+ years managing and developing software engineers.
  • Proven experience leading teams that build customer-installed applications, virtual appliances, connectors, gateways, or comparable software deployed in customer-managed environments.
  • Experience building software that securely connects customer environments with cloud-based SaaS services.
  • Strong technical understanding of Linux, virtualization, and containerization, with the ability to read and understand code and contribute meaningfully to architecture and design discussions.
  • Experience managing the lifecycle of customer-deployed software, including distribution, upgrades, patching, compatibility, diagnostics, vulnerability remediation, and incident response.
  • Demonstrated success implementing and refining Agile/Scrum practices to create predictable delivery while responding effectively to urgent needs.
  • Experience hiring, mentoring, managing performance, and supporting the career development of engineers.
  • Excellent planning, reporting, communication, and cross-functional coordination skills.
  • Experience leading distributed teams and collaborating effectively across time zones.
  • Hands-on fluency with modern AI and LLM tools, including experience using reusable skills and agents to achieve engineering and business outcomes and sound judgment about when an agent, skill, or conversational assistant is the right approach.
  • A strong product, customer, security, and reliability mindset.
  • Bachelor’s degree in a related field or equivalent professional experience.


The Tech Stack

  • Go and systems-oriented software development
  • Linux-based virtual appliances and multiple Linux distributions
  • Virtualization and container technologies
  • Modern AI and LLM tools, reusable skills, and agentic workflows

Overview of Position
The Senior Director, Program Management Lead for Commercial is responsible for leading integrated program management across the Commercial organization and ensuring Commercial priorities, milestones, dependencies, risks, and decisions are effectively coordinated with the broader enterprise program.

This role will partner closely with Commercial leadership and functional leads across Commercial, Market Access, Patient Services, Marketing, and other relevant functions, as well as key cross-functional partners such as Medical Affairs and the PMO. The Commercial Program Management Lead will own the integrated Commercial program and workstream plan and drive the planning, coordination, governance, and execution required to support commercialization and launch readiness.

The role will also oversee program management of launch-readiness activities, including management of external launch-readiness support as applicable, while Commercial and functional leaders retain accountability for commercial strategy, functional decisions, and deliverables.

As a senior member of the PMO organization, this individual will report to the Head of PMO and serve as the primary PMO partner to the Commercial organization.

Essential Duties
  • Own the integrated Commercial program and workstream plan, including key milestones, timelines, dependencies, risks, decisions, and critical-path activities across Commercial functions.
  • Lead integrated Commercial program management, connecting activities across Marketing, Market Access, Patient Services, Commercial Operations, and other relevant Commercial functions and cross-functional partners.
  • Drive launch-readiness program management and execution, ensuring readiness activities, decision points, dependencies, risks, and deliverables are integrated and actively managed across the organization.
  • Oversee external launch-readiness program management support and vendors, as applicable, to ensure alignment with company priorities, readiness criteria, timelines, and governance.
  • Integrate Commercial milestones and dependencies with the enterprise Integrated Program Plan, partnering with the Head of PMO and other Program Management Leads to maintain alignment across the broader program.
  • Establish and facilitate Commercial program governance, including leadership and cross-functional forums required to drive decisions, resolve issues, monitor readiness, and maintain execution against priorities.
  • Identify, manage, and escalate key program risks, dependencies, resource constraints, and decisions requiring Commercial or executive leadership attention.
  • Partner with Commercial leadership and functional leaders to translate strategic priorities and decisions into clear, executable plans while maintaining appropriate functional accountability.
  • Drive cross-functional coordination with key partner functions outside Commercial, including Medical Affairs and others, to ensure Commercial requirements and dependencies are identified and incorporated into program planning.
  • Provide clear and concise program reporting to senior leadership, including progress against critical milestones, launch readiness, emerging risks, decisions required, and areas requiring escalation.
  • Lead and/or oversee Commercial project management resources or other relevant vendors, as the organization evolves, ensuring consistent program management standards, tools, and ways of working.
  • Partner with the broader PMO organization to strengthen program governance, planning processes, tools, reporting, and execution discipline across Taysha.

Skill & Education Requirements
  • Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree such as an MBA, M.S., or other relevant graduate degree preferred.
  • 10+ years of experience in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or life sciences industry, with level commensurate with Senior Director or Executive Director responsibilities.
  • Significant experience in program/project management, commercialization, launch readiness, commercial operations, or a closely related cross-functional leadership role within the biopharmaceutical industry.
  • Demonstrated experience supporting late-stage development through commercialization and product launch, preferably within specialty, rare disease, advanced therapy, or similar complex therapeutic areas.
  • Strong understanding of the activities and interdependencies required for commercialization, including Marketing, Market Access, Patient Services, Commercial Operations, Medical Affairs, and related functions.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead complex, cross-functional programs in which functional leaders retain decision-making and deliverable accountability.
  • Experience developing and managing integrated program plans, including critical paths, milestones, dependencies, risks, decisions, and launch-readiness criteria.
  • Strong executive presence and demonstrated ability to work effectively with senior and executive leadership, facilitate decision-making, and appropriately escalate issues.
  • Demonstrated success operating in a fast-paced, dynamic, and evolving organization, with the ability to create structure, establish priorities, and drive execution through ambiguity.
  • Exceptional communication, facilitation, organizational, and stakeholder-management skills.
  • Ability to influence effectively across organizational boundaries and build strong partnerships across functional teams without relying on direct authority.
  • Experience managing project/program management personnel and/or external program management or commercialization vendors preferred.
  • PMP or other relevant program management certification preferred but not required.

This role can be performed remotely or based from Chicago IL. Expected travel 25%

​​Looking for Philippines-based candidates

Compensation range:$1800-$2500 AUD / Monthly

Who We Are: At Hunt St, we help Australian companies hire top remote talent in the Philippines. For this role, you will be formally engaged as an Independent Contractor (ICA). We are not an outsourcing agency. All of our roles are 100% remote, so you’ll be able to work from home.

Who The Client Is:
Our client has been assisting Australians with their borrowing requirements for over 40 years. With access to a wide panel of both major bank and non-bank lenders, the team structures the right loan for the client's circumstances, both now, into the future and as those circumstances change.

Their experience spans residential, commercial and industrial finance, from a client's first home through to funding a multi-storey office build. They have worked through both boom and bust cycles, and they bring that depth to every loan proposal they put together.

They are focused on building long-term relationships with their clients and are currently scaling up their organisation to enable them to help more Australians get access to funding as quickly and as simply as possible.

Role Overview:

Our client is looking for an experienced parabroker to take full ownership of the application process, from documentation review through to lender submission and settlement.

This is a senior support role, not an entry point into the industry. The broker currently carries the operational load alongside client-facing work, and the purpose of this hire is to lift that load entirely so he can focus on writing new business and building the client pipeline. You will be expected to run the pipeline with minimal direction after an initial ramp-up period, which means prior parabroking experience is essential.

The role is primarily residential lending with occasional involvement in commercial files. This role does not provide credit advice or credit assistance to clients. All loan recommendations and final sign-off remain with the broker.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Manage the active loan pipeline end to end, tracking the status and next action on every deal in progress
  • Review client documentation for completeness and accuracy before anything reaches a lender, including that payslips, bank statements and other income evidence reconcile.
  • Prepare and compile loan applications, including lender forms, supporting documentation and submission packs
  • Liaise directly with lenders on submissions, queries, outstanding conditions and approvals
  • Draft client communications and run follow-ups on outstanding documents and information
  • Maintain accurate records in the client's CRM and aggregator platform
  • Provide general administrative support that reduces the broker's operational workload

Requirements

Must-Haves:

  • 2 years prior experience as a parabroker or in mortgage broker support, with hands-on ownership of the application process
  • Working knowledge of Australian residential lending: serviceability, supporting documentation standards, lender policy and submission requirements
  • Experience with an Australian aggregator or broking CRM platform
  • High accuracy under volume, with a system for tracking multiple applications at different stages
  • Strong written English, suitable for direct correspondence with lenders and clients
  • Able to work independently and drive a pipeline forward without being prompted

Nice-to-Have:

  • Experience supporting a single broker or small brokerage rather than a large processing team
  • Exposure to complex or non-standard lending scenarios such as self-employed borrowers and alt-doc applications across both residential and commercial
  • Interest in growing beyond the processing function into a broader operational or leadership role

Professional and Personal Growth:

The business is growing, and the role grows with it. Depending on where your strengths and ambitions sit, there is scope to move into team leadership, marketing, or wider operational ownership over time. You will have an opportunity to work across multiple disciplines in the business to give you a feel for the development pathway you would like to own. The organisation is fully supportive in investing in their talent to grow and develop their skills.

Benefits

This is a remote, full-time role that will be set up as an independent contractor engagement.

To ensure alignment and transparency, successful candidates will be expected to:

  • Be available for meetings and collaboration during core AEST/AEDT business hours.
  • Disclose any existing ongoing roles or client work.
  • Reflect this engagement on their LinkedIn profile (clearly marked as “Independent Contractor”).

  • The HTA-Analyst, NAVLIN Market Access & HTA Consulting position will be responsible for delivering client consultancy projects focused on key business needs. Utilizing data and tools available through our industry platforms, NAVILN Price & Data and NAVLIN HTA Database, and enriching them with tailored insight and custom research. The Analyst will ensure that client projects are delivered to schedule, while maintaining the highest level of quality and value expectations.
  • As an HTA-Analyst, you will support research and lead analysis focused on: Payer (HTA) landscape mapping, HTA submissions, GVD development/Value demonstration & proposition, developing and supporting execution of early scientific advice plans, value-based pricing analyses, and more
  • The opportunity for growth is limitless. Effective Analyst will be able to develop and grow outside of project work and help support business development through the identification of leads, development of proposals/kickoff decks, and ability to create and engage with client relations.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Our Analysts are tasked with delivering excellent business results through the efforts of the project team. These results are achieved by:

  • Background in Health technology assessment, HEOR, Market access and reimbursement policies to effectively support HTA consulting projects for key clients.
  • Collaborate with other team members, including both internal and external resources in the design, development, and delivery of client deliverables.
  • Collaborates with other team members to provide the initial development of client reports and presentations and delivery of all or significant portions of findings to clients.
  • Leveraging business experience and acumen in identifying strategic alternatives and project approach to client questions. You will have a solution-oriented approach and look to add client value wherever possible.
  • Experience using analogues and secondary data (e.g., clinical guidelines, HTA outcomes, and raw pricing data) to inform HTA, reimbursement, and market access strategies.
  • Develop broader and deeper knowledge of consulting methodologies and pharmaceutical market through on-the-job experience and training.
  • High attention to quality and detail with strong written and spoken language. Excellent PowerPoint and Excel skills, able to present information in compelling and creative ways (story telling through data, insights, effective slides).

The above list reflects the general details necessary to describe the expectations of the position and shall not be construed as the only expectations that may be assigned for the position.

An individual in this position must be able to successfully perform the expectations listed above.

MINIMUM KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

  • Post-graduate degree in Pharmacy/Public Health/Health economics/Medicine/Lifesciences in relevant field of study required.
  • 1 to 4 years of experience in the market access / HEOR / HTA consulting setting
  • Demonstrates self-awareness and accountability
  • Self-starter with positive demeanor, creative thinking skills, ability to quickly build relationships and derive clear decisions and directives from ambiguity
  • Strong communication skills with ability to present complex messages and trade-offs and tell a compelling story
  • Understanding of pharmaceutical business practices and the issues clients face in specific segments of responsibility
  • Knowledge of global reimbursement and HTA requirements
  • Working knowledge of the Market Research Development process
  • Quantitative and qualitative market research skills
  • Proficiency in MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook
  • Ability to utilize large amounts of data and other types of information from multiple sources to complete a final analysis of a business question/situation and make recommendations
  • Ability to work under pressure and meet project deadlines
  • Creative approach and demonstrated client focus
  • Strong Problem-Solving Capabilities, Detail oriented, analytical and inquisitive.

Post-graduate degree in Pharmacy/Public Health/Health economics/Medicine/Lifesciences

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

jobs.description:
Social Media Manager – Remote

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Working Hours: U.S. Business Hours

About the Role

At Pavago, one of our clients is hiring a Social Media Manager to own and grow the company’s presence across multiple social media platforms.

This is not a scheduling-only role. We’re looking for someone who genuinely lives and breathes social media—someone who understands platform culture, creates content that feels native to each channel, and knows how to build engaged online communities.

From day one, you’ll take ownership of 10 social media accounts, beginning with a comprehensive account audit and strategic improvement plan. You’ll then execute platform-specific content strategies, create engaging short-form content, manage community engagement, and optimize performance across LinkedIn, X (Twitter), StockTwits, YouTube, TikTok, Facebook, Instagram, Reddit, Bluesky, and Pinterest.

If you understand that what performs on LinkedIn is very different from what succeeds on TikTok, Reddit, or StockTwits—and can adapt accordingly—this role is for you.

Responsibilities

Social Media Strategy & Account Audits

  • Conduct comprehensive audits of existing social media accounts and identify growth opportunities.
  • Develop platform-specific content strategies aligned with audience behavior and business objectives.
  • Create and maintain structured content calendars across all active platforms.
  • Identify content gaps, engagement opportunities, and audience growth strategies.
  • Continuously refine social strategies based on platform trends and performance data.

Social Media Management

  • Manage and publish content across:
    • LinkedIn
    • X (Twitter)
    • StockTwits
    • YouTube
    • TikTok
    • Facebook
    • Instagram
    • Reddit
    • Bluesky
    • Pinterest
  • Monitor comments, direct messages, mentions, and community engagement daily.
  • Adapt messaging, tone, and content style for each platform’s audience.
  • Maintain a consistent publishing schedule and brand voice across all channels.

Content Creation & Video Production

  • Create and edit short-form videos for TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts.
  • Design graphics and visual assets using Canva or similar design tools.
  • Produce engaging, platform-native content optimized for reach and engagement.
  • Repurpose content effectively across channels without making it feel repetitive.
  • Collaborate with internal teams to develop compelling marketing content.

Community Growth & Engagement

  • Grow social media accounts through authentic community engagement.
  • Participate in conversations across Reddit, StockTwits, and other relevant communities.
  • Monitor trends, industry conversations, and emerging content formats.
  • Build audience trust through meaningful interactions and timely responses.
  • Strengthen brand awareness and online community engagement.

Performance Optimization & Reporting

  • Boost high-performing content using native promotion tools across Meta, LinkedIn, TikTok, and other platforms.
  • Manage small paid budgets to amplify top-performing posts.
  • Analyze engagement, reach, audience growth, and conversion metrics.
  • Prepare regular performance reports with actionable recommendations.
  • Continuously optimize content strategy using platform analytics and campaign insights.

What Makes You a Great Fit

  • You genuinely enjoy social media outside of work.
  • You understand how platform culture differs across channels.
  • You combine creativity with data-driven decision-making.
  • You can manage multiple accounts while maintaining quality and consistency.
  • You adapt quickly to trends, platform updates, and audience behavior.
  • You understand B2B, SaaS, finance, or investor-focused communication.

Required Experience & Skills

Must-Have Qualifications

  • Proven experience managing multiple social media accounts simultaneously.
  • Strong background in B2B, SaaS, finance, or investor-focused social media marketing.
  • Demonstrated success growing engagement and building online communities.
  • Strong short-form video creation and editing skills.
  • Experience managing:
    • LinkedIn
    • X (Twitter)
    • Reddit
    • Instagram
    • Facebook
    • TikTok
    • YouTube
  • Experience conducting social media audits and developing actionable content strategies.
  • Experience boosting and promoting content using native platform tools.
  • Strong understanding of platform-native content and audience behavior.
  • Excellent written and verbal English communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience with Meta Ads Manager, LinkedIn Campaign Manager, or Google Ads.
  • Familiarity with HubSpot or Asana.
  • Experience working with investor-focused brands or financial audiences.
  • Experience managing StockTwits, Bluesky, and Pinterest communities.

Tools & Platforms

Candidates should already be comfortable using:

  • LinkedIn
  • X (Twitter)
  • StockTwits
  • YouTube
  • TikTok
  • Facebook
  • Instagram
  • Reddit
  • Bluesky
  • Pinterest
  • Canva (or similar design tools)
  • HubSpot or Asana
  • Native promotion tools across Meta, LinkedIn, and TikTok

What Success Looks Like

  • Consistent audience and engagement growth across all social platforms.
  • High-performing short-form content that increases visibility and reach.
  • Strong community interaction and authentic audience engagement.
  • Consistent, high-quality publishing across all managed accounts.
  • Clear reporting and continuous optimization based on performance analytics.
  • Increased brand awareness and stronger online communities.

Interview Process

  • Initial Phone Screen
  • Interview with Pavago Recruiter
  • Client Interview
  • Offer & Background Verification

What Happens After You Apply

Right after you apply, you’ll receive an email invitation from Spark Hire to record your Intro Video. This short, self-recorded video is the final step that completes your application.

Instead of repeating yourself across multiple screening calls, you’ll introduce yourself once, and your video will be shared with the hiring team. This helps hiring managers evaluate your communication style early, making future interviews more meaningful while reducing unnecessary interview rounds.

Don’t overthink it—you can record your video as many times as you’d like before submitting it. Only your final submission will be reviewed. Please keep an eye on both your inbox and spam folder for your Spark Hire invitation.

Apply Now

If you’re passionate about social media, understand how different platforms require different strategies, enjoy creating engaging content, and thrive on building online communities, we’d love to hear from you. Apply today and help grow a dynamic, high-impact social media presence across multiple digital channels.

jobs.description:
If you are currently on Young Life staff, please do not apply through this external jobs board. To apply for internal job opportunities, log in to Workday and use the Jobs Hub. Applying externally may delay your application and require you to resubmit internally.

Because of Young Life’s exclusive Christian purposes of evangelism and discipleship as set forth in its Articles of Incorporation and in these Bylaws, and to reflect what has always been and will continue to be the position of Young Life, specifically the Christian belief that each and every employee and volunteer of the corporation should minister as a servant of God with the primary responsibility of proclaiming the gospel of Jesus Christ and, as such, is an integral part of the Christian mission and ministry of the corporation,
Young Life shall only employ individuals or enlist volunteer leaders who: (a) profess a belief in Jesus Christ as their personal Savior and Lord; and (b) subscribe to the statements and policies required of all Young Life staff, including the Young Life Statement of Faith. Therefore, employees and volunteers of Young Life, during working and nonworking hours, shall: (i) be ready, willing and able to fulfill such ministry functions as may be required by the organization; (ii) refrain from conduct and statements that detract from the biblical standards taught and supported by Young Life, and (iii) abide by all policies and practices of Young Life including, without limitation, those related to religious belief or ministry activities.

All camps share a common purpose: creating an environment where Young Life staff bring Ch​rist to life by creatively​ presenting the complete gospel of Jesus Christ. Speaking clearly from the Scriptures, camp speakers introduce kids to the person of Christ, the nature of humanity, the work of Christ on the cross, the hope of the resurrection and the opportunity for reconciliation with God.

Young Life requires all​ employees to sign a Statement of Faith. We recommend you read this statement before applying​ for any position.

Camping Commitment Statement

As a follower of Jesus Christ and a minister of His gospel, lead from a mastery-level understanding of Young Life’s ministry strategy and ensure that all camp staff are supported and equipped in providing excellent camping experiences for individuals to encounter Jesus Christ and know the truth of God’s love for them.

Mission and Authority

Through both formal training and direct experience, learn how to effectively carry out and manage the responsibilities of the role, as a Camping divisional coordinator. This position is responsible for the operation and development of existing camps within their division, managing the operation start up for new camps, partnering with field SVPs, construction and development staff on construction projects, donor relations, finance, assuring spiritual care of staff, and otherwise representing the Camping department in the division to which assigned and other divisions that are supervised. This position functions as a team member with the other Camping divisional coordinators, the Camping Services coordinator, the camp staff training and development coordinator and the vice president of Camping and their staff members to direct the operations of the camps. This position partners with the senior field vice presidents of the divisions they supervise to respond to the current camping needs of the field and strategic development and identification of future needs.

Essential Prerequisites for all staff members (from Young Life’s Bylaws – Article VII):

“Because of Young Life’s exclusive Christian purposes of evangelism and discipleship as set forth in its Articles of Incorporation and in these Bylaws, and to reflect what has always been and will continue to be the position of Young Life, specifically the Christian belief that each and every employee and volunteer of the corporation should minister as a servant of God with the primary responsibility of proclaiming the gospel of Jesus Christ and, as such, is an integral part of the Christian mission and ministry of the corporation, Young Life shall only employ individuals or enlist volunteer leaders who: (a) profess a belief in Jesus Christ as their personal Savior and Lord; and (b) subscribe to the statements and policies required of all Young Life staff, including the Young Life Statement of Faith. Therefore, employees and volunteers of Young Life, during working and nonworking hours, shall: (i) be ready, willing and able to fulfill such ministry functions as may be required by the organization; (ii) refrain from conduct and statements that detract from the biblical standards taught and supported by Young Life, and (iii) abide by all policies and practices of Young Life including, without limitation, those related to religious belief or ministry activities.”

Essential Duties:

Mission and Methods:

  • Help ensure the health, safety and security of all guests and staff as the Mission, Vision, Values and Methods of Young Life are implemented at camps within the division supervised.

Spiritual Formation:Intentionally provide opportunities for staff to grow deeper in their relationship with Jesus.

  • Demonstrate a deep relationship with Jesus, a commitment to spiritual formation and an understanding of your personal ministry to others.

  • With support from supervisor, develop an annual personal spiritual growth plan by utilizing the Individual Development Plan for yourself and ensure that all staff are developing an annual spiritual growth plan as well.

  • Foster an environment where camp managers have opportunities for ongoing spiritual development, including execution of their personal spiritual growth plan.

  • Call staff and volunteers to the common vision for individuals to encounter Jesus and know the truth of God’s love for them.

  • Uphold and live out the CLT covenant commitments and practices.

  • Perform sacerdotal duties, as appropriate.

Attentive Hospitality:Equip servant leaders who anticipate and respond to the needs of our guests, staff and vendors, through Christlike service.

  • Ensure each camp within the division has an established culture of service and facility preparation that anticipates guest needs and responds with professionalism through intentional decisions and systems.

  • Demonstrate an understanding that hospitality is an essential role of the Camping department.

  • Convey to supervised camps any operational issues discussed and acted upon by the Camping Leadership Team.

  • Ensure camp managers are practicing attentive hospitality with camp directors, camp committee members and divisional SVP.

Interpersonal Relationships: Help build relationships that reflect the character of God with guests, staff, vendors and neighbors to foster healthy community.

·Build relationships that reflect the character of God with guests, staff, vendors and neighbors to foster healthy community.

  • Ensure camp staff demonstrate the importance of their interpersonal relationships with guests, staff, vendors and neighbors and promote a healthy community.

  • Develop strategies to solicit feedback from principle field staff who utilize different camps. Attend at least one camp committee meeting a year for a camp.

  • Build and equip a team that reflects the worldwide body of Christ.

  • Collaborate with the field senior vice president, vice president of Camping, regional directors, and area staff on all matters involving use of camps as an environment where the gospel is proclaimed.

  • Ensure camp managers are partnering with their camp’s committee in order to hear and appropriately respond to the concerns and desires of the Young Life staff they represent.

  • Participate with national leadership and peers in training events and opportunities.

Comprehensive Stewardship: Manage with integrity the finances, people, buildings and equipment that have been entrusted to our ministry.

  • Manage with integrity the finances, people, and camps that have been entrusted to our ministry.

  • Ensure camp managers and other supervised staff are being developed and equipped to participate in comprehensive stewardship of our ministry.

  • As a participant in mission leadership, determine fundraising priorities and funds for the further capital development of camps.

  • Ensure every camp manager’s cultivation and maintenance of donor relationships is in collaboration with Young Life’s development team.

  • Partner with the development committee or individual for each camp as established by the appropriate senior field vice president, maintaining appropriate donor relations for supervised camps.

  • Carry out the responsibilities of supervising the operations manager of a camp if a camp manager is not separately assigned. This includes affiliate camp managers, if they are not specifically assigned to a different camp manager.

  • Oversee, audit and sign off on each supervised camp’s five-year plan and its annual update. This includes major maintenance planning and expansion planning.

  • Establish and facilitate a divisional leadership team that conducts meetings on at least a monthly basis.

  • Work with the director of construction to facilitate and determine the Primary Mission Projects for each camp supervised. Assist in different phases of capital construction planning. This involves the coordination of the specific camp’s operations and logistics impacted by the new project and construction, partnering with the Development department (timing and cash flow of gifts) and on-site project management.

  • Manage and evaluate comprehensive stewardship in partnership with Camping Services.

Talent Development: Through a consistent and accountable evaluation process, we identify and provide opportunities for staff in continuing education, leadership development, career-pathing and cross-training.

  • Demonstrate a desire to grow through engagement in the Individual Development Plan process and participation in training and development opportunities.

  • Foster divisional camp staff participation in the Individual Development Plan process as well as other training and development opportunities.

  • Identify and develop staff suitable for additional leadership opportunities.

  • Intentionally pursue opportunities in mission leadership, personal growth and development.

  • Execute the recruitment, hiring and onboarding process for building a diverse and qualified team.

  • Work with the senior vice president of Camping to establish Camping Leadership Team meeting and Camping Summit schedules and associated agendas. This includes leading portions of these meetings and/or associated conference and video calls.

  • Train or arrange training for supervised camp managers on specific duties and responsibilities they are not familiar with, as well as for new methods or procedures that may be adopted by the department. This includes onboarding new camp managers.

  • Ensure completion and documentation of annual performance evaluations and salary reviews with all staff.

Embracing Excellence: Standing on the platform of national standards and metrics, we gladly prepare an environment that glorifies Jesus Christ.

  • Ensure divisional camp planning and operations are consistent with the national board and Camping department policies and are within the standards and metrics required for excellence.

  • When Young Life is searching for another camp, participate as defined by the new camp development matrix.

  • Annually lead and participate in the camp calendar and analysis process to estimate and predict future camping trends and opportunities, including the right-sizing of camp schedules for the future.

  • Review, comment on and be responsible for the timely submittal of documents by each supervised entity to the Camping Services office and/or other authorities, including, but not limited to: financial reports, personnel actions, master plan and fundraising priority information, camp dates, allocation of camp spots, and staffing for work crew, summer staff and assignment team staffing.

  • Coordinate and work with the senior vice president of Camping to schedule periodic visits to all camps supervised to inspect quality, be available to the staff and consult with other coordinators and managers.

  • Provide reports to the senior vice president of Camping as requested.

  • Participate as a member of Young Life’s Camping Leadership Team and other mission responsibilities as assigned.

  • Participate with other coordinators and the senior vice president of Camping in formulating new policies and procedures for the department and obtain understanding, acceptance and support of these policies and procedures from and camp managers for whom responsible.

  • Ensure compliance with governmental agencies whose jurisdiction affect camp operations.

  • Cast vision and set the pace for a healthy attitude and commitment to continuous improvement of the camp environment.

  • Ensure the creation of distraction-free environments that represent the multi-faceted love of God through the quality of facilities and the camp experience.

Camp or Job Specific Working Conditions:

  • See Local Operations Procedure document for additional duties.

Education:

  • Four-year college degree required

Training Expectations:

  • Ability and willingness to travel at least 12 times a year

Qualifications and Experience Required for the Job:

  • At least three years of general management and supervisory experience.

  • Demonstrate thorough knowledge and effective involvement in ministry.

  • Has proven leadership and relationship skills required to build a high-performing trusting team, communicate effectively, delegate responsibility and offer accountability.

  • Demonstrate operational disciplines including prioritizing, analyzing data, and developing and executing systems.

  • Exhibition of a mastery understanding in the Young Life mission and camping operational policies.

This description is not intended, and should not be construed, to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, skills, efforts or working conditions associated with this job. It is intended to be an accurate reflection of the principal job elements essential for making compensation decisions.

Notes:

Young Life is a relational ministry. Staff must be able to convey a sense of Christ-like hospitality and concern for guests and staff. Responding to the unexpected needs of a guest in a prompt and professional manner is important. All staff members are expected to represent Young Life positively and professionally within the community and be able to work with and minister to the volunteer high school and college-age young people who attend our camp.

Job Specific Working Conditions:


Working Specific Conditions

  • This position requires you to work remotely within the Southeastern Division, which includes Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, or Tennessee.
  • You can expect approximately 25% travel, including travel for ministry engagement, meetings, training, and other organizational activities.

Pay Transparency

In the U.S., the standard base pay range for this role is outlined below. This base pay range is for the U.S. and is not applicable to locations outside of the United States.

The anticipated salary rate for this position can range from $98,200-$136,000depending on relevant education, experience, and location.

jobs.description:
About Engine

Engine is the all-in-one travel and spend management platform trusted by 38K+ businesses and groups representing 1.8M+ travelers. We're the retailer and the rails of business travel, one of the fastest-growing companies in travel tech, built on a decade of proprietary technology, supply, and pricing no one else can replicate. Other travel and AI companies run on our infrastructure to book real trips, hold rates, and move payments, without building any of it themselves. We built it, AI-forward at every layer, from how travelers book to how the rails run.

That work has earned recognition as one of Fast Company's Best Workplaces for Innovators (2025), TravelTech's Reservation Platform of the Year (2026), and one of Built In's Best Places to Work (2020–2026).

We're looking for bold, ambitious people to help redefine how businesses manage and experience travel. Working here, you can expect exponential growth, an ambitious pace, full ownership, and high-caliber colleagues who push you to do the best work of your career. Every hire raises the bar.

Come outpace the ordinary and build the future of travel with us.

Your Mission

As Engine scales, our in-person moments matter more, not less. We're looking for a highly organized, detail-driven Internal Events Coordinator to help us build a world-class in-person experience for a remote-first team, supporting everything from vendor management and registration to the marketing and comms that get people in the room.

You'll be the engine behind our internal events, the person who turns a plan into a flawless, memorable experience. Partnering closely with our Employee Experience and Events lead, you'll own the details, vendors, registration, and communications that make every offsite, summit, and town hall come together seamlessly.

The Role

  • Event Logistics & Vendor Management: Support planning and execution for Engine's off sites, annual org summits, and quarterly in-person town halls. Coordinate and manage vendors [ie: venues, catering, travel, AV, and swag] to bring every event to life.
  • Registration & Attendee Experience: Own registration, RSVPs, and check-in for internal events, making sure every attendee has a smooth experience from invite to arrival.
  • Event Marketing & Communications: Partner with internal comms to build and send event invites, reminders, and recaps that drive excitement and turnout across a distributed workforce.
  • Playbook & Process Support: Help build and refine repeatable playbooks for Engine's in-person programs, capturing what works so every event gets sharper than the last.
  • Automation & Product Impact: Continuously look for opportunities to automate workflows, improve processes, and provide actionable feedback to our Product teams, leveraging our unique position as power users of our own platform to shape a better experience for both internal teams and customers.
  • On-the-Ground Execution: Travel on-site as needed (2-3 times per quarter) to support setup, run-of-show, and real-time problem-solving so events run without a hitch.
  • Company Swag: Own the strategy and execution for internal swag programs (new hires, milestones, and special events), managing our online swag store vendor to ensure high-quality fulfillment, seamless logistics, and memorable team celebrations.

Who You Are

  • Detail-Obsessed Executor: No detail is too small. You catch what others miss and follow through until it's done.
  • Vendor-Savvy Coordinator: You know how to direct and partner with vendors on-site to ensure seamless execution, while keeping the bigger picture in focus.
  • Clear Communicator: You write crisp, on-brand invites and updates that get people excited to show up.
  • Calm Under Pressure: Event-day chaos doesn't rattle you, you adapt in real time and keep things moving.
  • Collaborative Partner: You build trust fast with vendors, DRIs, and teammates across the company.

Qualifications

  • 1–3+ years of experience in event coordination, hospitality, administrative support, or related field
  • Experience managing vendors, venues, and event budgets
  • Strong written communication skills; comfortable owning comms tied to events
  • Proficiency with event registration/RSVP tools and project management tools
  • Hands-on experience managing online swag stores and/or corporate merchandise programs
  • Highly organized with excellent attention to detail and an eye for design

jobs.title: STRIDES Laboratory and Diagnostics Advisor, Outbreak Preparedness and Response
jobs.excerpt: Job SummaryThe Laboratory and Diagnostics Advisor provides technical guidance and support for United States Government (USG)-funded STRIDES’ outbreak response and preparedness laboratory and diagnostic systems portfolio, leading efforts to expand, validate, and strengthen diagnostic capacity while reinforcing national laboratory systems for long‑term preparedness.
jobs.description:
Job Summary

The Laboratory and Diagnostics Advisor provides technical guidance and support for United States Government (USG)-funded STRIDES’ outbreak response and preparedness laboratory and diagnostic systems portfolio, leading efforts to expand, validate, and strengthen diagnostic capacity while reinforcing national laboratory systems for long‑term preparedness. As a core member of the STRIDES technical team, the Advisor supports outbreak response countries, including for the current Ebola outbreak, and regional preparedness contexts by guiding diagnostic network strengthening, laboratory readiness, biosafety and biosecurity, quality systems, and workforce development.

The role ensures that diagnostic assays, platforms, algorithms, and procurement align with national policies, outbreak response plans, and international standards; oversees laboratory and diagnostics activities and subcontractor implemented activities; and works closely with ministries of health, national public health institutes, reference laboratories, and other technical team members to ensure a coordinated, technically coherent approach across the STRIDES outbreak response and preparedness portfolio. Reporting to the STRIDES Senior Laboratory and Diagnostics Advisor, the Advisor ensures that emergency laboratory investments translate into sustainable, government‑owned diagnostic systems capable of supporting routine public health functions and future outbreak response.

Accountabilities

Technical Requirements:

  • Provides technical leadership for STRIDES’ outbreak laboratory and diagnostic systems portfolio, guiding the design and implementation of diagnostic capacity, laboratory network strengthening, biosafety and biosecurity, quality systems, and workforce development.

  • Works on moderate to complex laboratory systems challenges requiring evaluation of multiple technical, operational, and contextual factors—including diagnostic algorithm optimization, specimen referral systems, decentralized testing models, and national laboratory governance.

  • Demonstrates strong judgment in selecting diagnostic methods, technologies, and evaluation criteria; advises on assay validation, platform selection, and alignment of procurement with nationally approved workflows.

  • Networks and collaborates with key internal and external personnel, including ministries of health, national public health institutes, reference laboratories, STRIDES technical team members, implementing partners, and regional preparedness stakeholders.

  • Interprets laboratory readiness findings, quality system gaps, biosafety risks, and diagnostic performance data; recommends evidence‑based improvements across specimen handling, testing workflows, reporting systems, and laboratory surge operations.

  • Provides input to senior technical leadership on national laboratory policies, essential diagnostics lists, specimen referral strategies, laboratory governance mechanisms, and outbreak diagnostic guidelines.

  • Performs other duties as assigned to advance STRIDES’ outbreak response and Global Health Security objectives.

Project Design Implementation:

  • With technical oversight, provides leadership in the design, development, planning, and implementation of laboratory and diagnostic components of STRIDES projects, ensuring alignment with national priorities, outbreak response needs, and international standards.

  • Leads the creation of the laboratory and diagnostics technical portion of project plans, incorporating diagnostic network strengthening, biosafety and biosecurity, quality management systems, workforce development, and reference laboratory capacity building.

  • Oversees day‑to‑day laboratory and diagnostic activities in assigned response and preparedness countries, including readiness assessments, deployment of diagnostic platforms, optimization of testing algorithms, and strengthening of specimen referral and transport systems.

  • Tracks delivery of laboratory‑related project outputs, ensuring activities are implemented on time, within budget, and consistent with STRIDES’ technical approach and donor requirements.

  • Monitors staff members’ LOE to ensure adequate technical coverage across laboratory readiness, diagnostic operations, biosafety mentorship, quality systems strengthening, and reference laboratory support.

  • Coordinates requests from country offices for laboratory technical assistance, ensuring coherent and timely support across response and preparedness contexts.

  • Leads the design and implementation of global‑level innovative technical strategies for outbreak diagnostics, decentralized testing, laboratory governance, biosafety and biosecurity, and diagnostic network optimization.

  • Maintains constructive dialogue and technical exchange with field counterparts, national laboratory authorities, reference laboratories, and implementing partners to ensure coordinated, high‑quality laboratory system strengthening.

  • Develops tools, guidance, and job aids that support the design and implementation of laboratory and diagnostic components, including readiness assessment tools, diagnostic algorithm job aids, and quality systems strengthening instruments.

  • Ensures laboratory and diagnostic implementation is consistent with international best practices, national policies, and STRIDES’ technical standards; verifies that diagnostic workflows, biosafety measures, and quality systems meet client and funder contractual obligations across one or more major functional areas.

  • May supervise junior technical staff, Laboratory/Diagnostics Officers, subcontractors, and consultants implementing laboratory activities; provides oversight to ensure coherent, high‑quality execution of diagnostic network strengthening, biosafety mentorship, and quality systems support.

  • Functions in an advisor capacity with oversight of technical project administration, finance compliance, technical deliverables, and team management across laboratory and diagnostic components, including subcontractor implemented work.

  • Leads daily laboratory and diagnostic activities for assigned projects, including diagnostic platform deployment, specimen referral system strengthening, biosafety and biosecurity support, and quality management system improvements.

  • Tracks delivery of laboratory‑related project outputs, ensuring timely, high‑quality completion of diagnostic readiness assessments, algorithm optimization, biosafety improvements, and quality system strengthening activities.

Partner/Sub-Award Management:

  • May serve as a daily POC (Point of Contact) with clients for some projects on technical matters.

Capacity Building, Training and Supervision:

  • Develops and implements technical training and capacity building interventions.

  • Identifies strategies to address training gaps.

  • May supervise or provide technical guidance to staff members.

Operations Management (Finance, HR, etc.):

  • Manages the processes, services, planning, organizing, coordinating, and controlling of all technical resources for a project.

Project/Program Reporting:

  • Drafts sponsor financial and technical reports.

  • Collates and uploads output and deliverables data to sponsor data systems. Prepares and delivers presentations to sponsors on progress.

  • Helps in the development and review of work plans.

  • Creates technical content, owning the content, true experts at an advanced level (may be the most senior technical person).

  • Serves as the primary author for technical deliverables (e.g., reports, presentations, manuscripts).

  • Gathers and aggregates data to provide a summary / high level overview.

Quality Assurance:

  • Ensures technical deliverables are consistent with best practices in the industry / subject and meet client/funder contractual obligations.

  • Identifies areas for improved efficiency or effectiveness within prescribed parameters, and institutes enhancements to procedures.

Applied Knowledge & Skills

  • Ensures appropriate and timely technical support for field projects.

  • Ensures the quality of implemented technical activities and systems at all levels. Conducts routine coordination with employees and consultants, on-site and in the field.

  • Strong knowledge and skills in a specific technical area/function and general understanding of concepts and principles of related technical areas/functions.

  • Solid knowledge of standards for the technical area/field, operational processes and procedures, work, and task flow.

  • Has the ability to manage projects, set realistic priorities, and plan for the successful implementation of activities.

  • Proficient writing and verbal communication skills.

  • Relevant computer software skills (including, at a minimum, the standard applications in MS Office).

  • Ability to manage their own work to job and performance standards.

  • Must be able to read, write and speak fluent English fluent in host country language.

Problem Solving & Impact

  • Demonstrates the ability to assess needs within agreed upon duties and considers course of action best to meet those needs.

  • Effectively applies knowledge of technical area to solve a range of problems. Demonstrates the ability to develop solutions to problems that cannot be solved using existing methods or approaches.

  • Faulty decisions/recommendations/failures to complete assignments will normally resultiserious delays to assigned projects resulting in considerable expenditure of additional time, resources, and funds.

  • Decisions and actions impact primarily workflow, project processes and timeframes. Problems encountered are valid, requiring review of practices and precedents to resolve. Problem solving involves evaluating and resolving discrepancies with data, analyses, processes within prescribed guidelines.

  • Policies or guidelines exist for most problems; others must be referred to by a supervisor or more senior professional.

Supervision Given/Received

  • May supervise junior staff members.

  • Coordinates own workflow and sets individual priorities.

  • Works under general guidelines for completion and accuracy as determined by the supervisor.

  • May manage a centralized functional area of activity. Serves as mentor to technical staff.

Education

  • Master’s Degree or an International Equivalent in Laboratory Science, Microbiology, Clinical Diagnostics, Public Health or a related clinical/medical field.

  • Project Management (PM) Certification preferred.

Experience

  • Typically requires 8+ years of relevant experience in implementing large-scale laboratory systems, networks, and diagnostics programs.

  • Emergency outbreak response experience/knowledge preferred.

  • Mentoring junior laboratory staff and guides technical activities.

  • Documented success providing systems-level laboratory guidance.

  • Proven track record training laboratory personnel, validating assays, and establishing quality management systems (QMS).

  • Experience designing laboratory strengthening portfolios, securing research or development grants, or driving public health program growth.

  • Prior work experience in a non-governmental organization (NGO), government agency, or private organization.

  • International or Domestic (US) Program Development or Program management preferred.

Typical Physical Demands

  • Typical office environment.

  • Ability to spend long hours looking at a computer screen and doing repetitive work on a keyboard.

  • Ability to sit and stand for extended periods of time. Ability to lift 5lb.

Technology to be Used

  • Personal Computer, Microsoft Office 365 (i.e., Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Skype/TEAMS, e-mail), office telephone, cell phone and printer/copier.

Travel Requirements

  • 10% - 25%

Are you passionate about technology and enjoy explaining complex solutions in a way that everybody gets excited? If so, read on!

Picus Security, the leading exposure validation company, proves what attackers can exploit and what your defenses stop, then closes real gaps with ready-to-deploy fixes and revalidates to confirm at the machine speed that today’s AI threats demand. The Picus Platform spans Picus Autonomous Penetration Testing, Picus Breach and Attack Simulation, and Picus Exposure Validation, unified by Picus Swarm, a swarm of AI agents that runs the whole validation loop continuously with human oversight. With 75+ integrations, it reaches across on-prem, hybrid cloud, and endpoint environments.

Trusted by many Fortune 500 enterprises, Picus was named a 2025 Gartner Peer Insights Customers’ Choice for Adversarial Exposure Validation and is recognized as an Innovation Leader in the Frost Radar for Automated Security Validation.

About The Role

If you're someone who takes initiative, forms your own point of view, and does your best work in a fast-moving environment, this is an opportunity to join a company that has consistently introduced new approaches to the market. We are looking for someone to take what Picus Labs and the product teams build and make it understandable and adoptable: translating research into language the field understands, and developing the mental models organizations need to evaluate and adopt new approaches.

Positioning at Picus is a team effort. You'll work closely with the CTO, the Product Marketing team, and cross-functional leaders; bringing your own well-formed point of view to the table, challenging assumptions constructively, and contributing to decisions rather than making them alone. Within that shared effort, you'll take ownership of specific deliverables end to end, from research and a strong first draft to the refined narrative the field actually uses and be accountable for their quality and impact.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role, with messaging, narratives, and executive-level presentations refreshed each quarter. It suits a strong communicator who enjoys the craft itself: doing the research, forming an opinion, writing well, and iterating quickly on feedback.

What You'll Do

  • Partner closely with the CTO and cross-functional leaders to continuously evolve Picus’ company, portfolio, and product positioning as the market and product strategy change
  • Monitor the cybersecurity market, Gartner and other key analysts, customer priorities, emerging categories, and competitor narratives to identify market shifts, differentiation opportunities, and strategic white space
  • Develop clear and differentiated messaging frameworks, value propositions, category narratives, and proof points for Picus and its evolving product portfolio
  • Translate complex product innovation and Picus Labs research into compelling, evidence-backed stories that resonate with customers, prospects, analysts, partners, and industry influencers
  • Lead the quarterly refresh of Picus’ corporate and portfolio narrative, including executive-level presentations for customers, the field, analysts, and major industry events
  • Shape Picus’ thought-leadership agenda and collaborate with internal experts to develop distinctive points of view, research reports, whitepapers, and executive or event narratives
  • Equip Sales and other go-to-market teams with messaging playbooks, presentations, competitive guidance, and launch narratives that help them communicate Picus’ value consistently and confidently
  • Validate and refine messaging through feedback from customers, prospects, analysts, and field teams, ensuring Picus’ positioning remains relevant, credible, and differentiated

What You Have

  • 5+ years of product marketing (or equivalent) experience in B2B enterprise software, including meaningful experience in cybersecurity
  • A proven track record of defining and evolving company, portfolio, and product positioning in fast-changing markets
  • Strong understanding of cybersecurity buyers, market categories, analyst perspectives, and competitive dynamics; experience in exposure management or security validation is a strong advantage
  • The ability to synthesize customer insight, competitive intelligence, analyst research, and technical innovation into original points of view and actionable strategic recommendations
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills in English, with the ability to simplify complex technical concepts without losing credibility or substance
  • Excellent storytelling and presentation skills, including experience developing executive-level narratives and presentations for customers, analysts, sales teams, and industry events
  • Strong executive presence and the ability to collaborate with—and constructively challenge—leaders across Product, Research, Sales, and Marketing
  • A hands-on, high-ownership working style, with the ability to move independently from research and strategy to a strong first draft, then iterate quickly based on feedback

Working at Picus

Fascinating work - a chance to shape and lead an exciting, fast-growing cyber security segment. Security Validation is a concept that helps organizations evaluate their security posture in a continuous, automated, and repeatable way. This approach allows for the identification of imminent threats, provides recommended actions, and produces valuable metrics about cyber-risk levels.
Unlimited opportunity! We are growing. At Picus, you'll be provided with as much responsibility as you can handle - new career development opportunities constantly arise given our rate of growth.
Global exposure - Get a lot of experience working not only in a fast-growing startup but also interact with customers all around the world.
Be part of a global remote team who is taking on Exposure Validation and a growing market segment.
